candidates.title: Governing Human-Centric AI in Healthcare
candidates.abstract: The debate about artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is no longer focused on whether AI will be used, but on how it should be governed. Across Europe and beyond, policymakers, healthcare organizations, and technology developers are searching for ways to ensure that AI systems remain accountable, transparent, and aligned with human values. The European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act represents one of the most ambitious attempts to address these challenges through a human-centric approach. Yet an important question remains unanswered: what does human-centric AI actually look like when organizations begin implementing AI technologies in practice? This book explores that question in the context of healthcare and humanoid robotics. Rather than examining regulation or technology in isolation, it brings together perspectives from AI governance, management, healthcare, and technology acceptance research. The discussion moves from the principles embedded in the AI Act to the realities of organizational decision-making, showing how ideas such as human dignity, human oversight, trust, inclusivity, and accountability influence the adoption of emerging technologies. A central theme running throughout the book is the gap between technological possibility and organizational readiness. Drawing on empirical research involving 527 respondents – current and future decision-makers, the book examines perceptions of humanoid robots in healthcare and identifies the factors that encourage or discourage their adoption. The findings reveal that acceptance is shaped not only by expected benefits but also by concerns about trust, responsibility, ethics, patient safety, and the preservation of human interaction in care. The book also proposes two original concepts: the Human-Centric Robot Acceptance Index (HCRAI), which evaluates readiness for humanoid robot adoption, and the Risk Gradient Model of Humanoid Robot Task Acceptance, which explains why some healthcare tasks are considered more suitable for robots than others. Together, these contributions offer new ways of understanding how AI technologies can be integrated into healthcare organizations while maintaining meaningful human oversight. Written for researchers, healthcare professionals, managers, policymakers, and students, this book provides an interdisciplinary perspective on one of the most important challenges facing contemporary healthcare: ensuring that technological innovation remains centered on people rather than technology itself.

candidates.title: Mechanism of AI chatbot anthropomorphism on consumer impulse buying in live streaming scenarios based on SOR framework
candidates.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into real-time e-commerce, it is necessary to study how AI virtual hosts affect consumers' immediate purchase decisions. This research is based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and explores the psychological mechanism by which the characteristics of AI hosts influence impulsive purchases. The scenario-based experiments show that AI anthropomorphism (ANT) and social conversation cues (SCC) affect impulsive purchases through two mediating states: cognitive trust and emotional arousal. The results indicate that the association between SCC and trust and arousal is stronger than that of visual anthropomorphism, and multiple group analyses show that this mechanism is roughly consistent across gender groups, but there are differences between the product participation and AI experience groups. This research expands upon previous work by testing visual and verbal anthropomorphic cues as parallel stimuli in live-streaming business, and provides guidance for the design of AI virtual hosts.

candidates.title: Blue mind, healthy life and well-being: the therapeutic benefits of coastal living in Ghana
candidates.abstract: Abstract Coastal environments are traditionally characterized by relaxation and wellness but are empirically short of therapeutic research on the health value in Ghana. The blue mind concept suggests that being near water is healthy and beneficial to well-being. This qualitative study investigates the psychological, physical, and social therapeutic benefits of coastal residents living in Akosua Village, Ghana, through the Blue Mind Theory, Biophilia Hypothesis, Social Capital Theory, Therapeutic Landscapes Theory and Ostrom’s Social-Ecological Systems (SES) Framework. By conducting in-depth interviews with 15 residents, the study reveals that proximity to the ocean decreases stress and anxiety significantly, improves mood, and improves cognitive functioning, which is in line with the Blue Mind Theory and the Biophilia Hypothesis. Habituation effects also decrease emotional benefits for long-term residents, suggesting variability in environmental sensitivity. The study further highlights the physical health advantages of living on the coast, including increased activity through swimming, fishing, and walking. Sleep quality in coastal settlements differs among participants; some residents report the ocean sounds restful, while others report a disturbance. Socially, the beach is a shared space, facilitating bonding through casual meetings and shared labor, following the Social Capital Theory. Moreover, traditional seawater treatments are also prevalent, with residents using them to heal illnesses like stomach disorders and skin conditions, justifying the Therapeutic Landscapes Theory. Despite these benefits, there is conflict between restorative leisure and economic output, with some residents viewing contemplative time as unnecessary and unproductive. The study recommends the integration of blue spaces into public health policy, promoting coastal therapy in mental health care, and further research on seawater treatments. Policy-makers have to balance communal beach access with managing sleeping environment noise sensitivity.

candidates.title: Integrating Agri-food in the SCPS: Exploring the Role of Digitalisation for Niche-Innovations in Collective Actions and the Impacts on Sustainability Dimensions—The Case of the PDO Parmigiano Reggiano
candidates.abstract: This chapter proposes a conceptualisation of the digitalisation in rural systems building on the analytical constructs of niche-innovation in agricultural ecosystems and socio-cyber-physical systems (SCPS). We submit that digitalisation acts as driving force of innovative niches, playing a role in incorporation of the agri-food in SCPSs. Niches are settings where social entities make use of digital technologies to trigger dynamics of co-experimentation and co-creation of novel practices in support of a sustainable transition pathways going beyond the existing socio-technical regime and contributing to Sustainable Development Goals. Focusing on a collective action, such as the PDO ‘Parmigiano Reggiano’ Protection Consortium (PRC), the analysis shows actors, networks and system’s relationships supporting a “digitalisation niche” and reveals connections at stake with sustainability indicators,

Integrating socio-emotional scaffolding into educational robotics: Effects on classroom climate in heterogeneous lower secondary schools
candidates.abstract: This study explores the impact of educational robotics activities explicitly designed to foster collaboration and inclusion on classroom climate. A quasi-experimental design was implemented in two rural schools, involving 47 students aged 11–12. The experimental group engaged in robotics sessions enriched with socio-emotional scaffolding, while the control group participated in technically comparable but socially neutral activities. Data were collected using the Classroom Climate Questionnaire and a student feedback survey. Results showed a significant improvement in perceived classroom climate in the experimental group, contrasted with a decline in the control group. Qualitative findings further revealed that experimental students described their experiences in a more competent way, without referring to frustration. These outcomes highlight the importance of embedding socio-emotional learning objectives into technology-enhanced instruction.

candidates.title: Food at the Hearth: Emotional Connections and Generational Transmission of Escudella i Carn d'Olla in Traditional Catalan Cuisine
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper analyses the changes and continuity in the preparation and rituals of escudella i carn d'olla , a manifestation of traditional Catalan cuisine. Based on interviews with 27 ordinary citizens from different generations, the research explores how they experience, elaborate, and emotionally relate to escudella i carn d'olla , and what generational and gender patterns can be identified in these relationships. Results show that one of the most notable aspects of escudella i carn d'olla is its role in family bonding, which is shared by the three generations—the dish as a symbol of a family ritual, which mostly happens in winter, and creates a shared feeling of warmth. In addition, the changing pace of life and new consumption patterns affect how family cooking is perceived and practiced. While for older generations, the preparation of escudella is an act of caring and love for the family, younger generations have lost interest in dedicating so much time to preparing it. Its traditional preparation reflects local supply systems—such as local butcher shops and markets—and embodies a female know‐how. Its value lies in its emotional significance as it represents a cultural and social connection to the past and the present, but also to the future.

candidates.title: Predictions and goals modulate use of partner's gaze during joint action with humanoid robots
candidates.abstract: During joint actions, partners coordinate attention and actions by using each other's gaze to predict upcoming actions and align with shared goals. Although gaze orienting has been extensively studied using screen-based paradigms, it remains unclear whether partner reliability and action goals calibrate the use of the partner's gaze during embodied interactions. We addressed this using a humanoid robot as a co-actor in two experiments. In Experiment 1, participants performed a color-sorting task while the robot provided informative or noninformative gaze cues. Cue reliability was manipulated between participants: one group experienced a robot whose gaze was informative in 80% of trials, and another at chance level. Task difficulty was manipulated within participants. Only the reliable group made fewer errors on valid than invalid trials under high-difficulty. In Experiment 2, participants completed a handover task in which an auditory cue established an action plan, the robot looked toward a goal-congruent or incongruent object, and a target appeared at a valid or invalid location. Participants responded faster at the cued location only when the robot looked toward the goal-matching object, with eye tracking confirming covert attentional shifts. Together, these findings show that the use of the partner's gaze in embodied joint action operates as a flexible, utility-weighting heuristic. Observers weighted gaze according to its value, upweighting gaze from a reliable partner and when it aligned with shared goals and down-weighting gaze that conflicted with predictions. These results advance understanding of gaze use as a predictive, context-dependent mechanism with implications for reliance on social signals during joint action with humans and artificial agents.

candidates.title: Automated detection of mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies of multi-party interactions
candidates.abstract: This article describes a data-processing pipeline for quantifying mutual gaze in mobile eye-tracking studies. Mutual gaze is defined as eye contact between participants who look at each other simultaneously. We applied the pipeline to data from dyadic and multi-party interactions (“quartets”). Using state-of-the-art computer vision tools for fiducial-marker tracking and face detection, the pipeline processes scene camera videos from TobiiPro eye-trackers to extract facial areas-of-interest (AOIs). Each participant's gaze samples are classified relative to visible co-participants, indicating when gaze is directed at another's face. By integrating multiple participants' high-resolution data streams, the pipeline identifies periods of unreciprocated (unilateral) gaze as well as mutual gaze. The output files contain time-stamped measures of gaze events and can be imported into the annotation tool ELAN for qualitative analysis. While processing is largely automated, some steps require validity checks by the researcher. To underpin our observations on the potential of the proposed pipeline for the automatic extraction of mutual gaze, we subsequently conduct an exploratory analysis on the participants' unilateral gaze and mutual gaze proportions in relation to the following factors: seating position, speaking proportion, age, gender, familiarity, and movement synchrony. The results show that speaking proportion, seating position, and familiarity were significantly associated with unilateral and mutual gaze proportion. By contrast, an association with age, gender, and movement synchrony measurements was not shown. The article concludes with a critical discussion of the limitations and strengths of the proposed pipeline. We highlight the opportunities and challenges of quantifying gaze patterns in complex multi-party settings with a specific interest on how existing qualitative and quantitative findings may be brought together for future studies.

candidates.title: The context of AI transformation: perceptions of AI ethicality and their impact on trust and use intentions
candidates.abstract: Introduction As the implementation of AI accelerates within organizations, concerns emerge about the ethicality of AI-driven systems and tools and the ways people use them. Although previous literature proposes numerous theories regarding how to develop and use AI ethically, questions remain about how users perceive the ethicality of AI and the effects this has on their engagement with AI tools. The study aims to explore whether and how certain perceptions of AI tool attributes, including beliefs about the explainability of the AI tool (xAI) and moral intensity dimensions (i.e., magnitude of consequences and proximity), influence perceptions of AI ethicality. Additionally, the study examines the effects of AI ethicality perceptions on the likelihood to recommend AI tools and functionality trust in AI. Methods Researchers employ a randomized, controlled study design to investigate the relationships between the antecedents, perceptions of AI ethicality, and outcomes of functionality trust and behavioral intention. Results Analyses revealed that AI ethicality perceptions significantly mediated the relationship between xAI and the likelihood to recommend the AI tool, whereas functionality trust in the AI tool significantly mediated the relationship between proximity and the likelihood to recommend the AI tool. Discussion The results indicate the strength of users’ beliefs about xAI on their perceptions of AI ethicality and how users perceive AI as less capable of making decisions for human decision recipients. The perceptual nature of the study provides a theoretical contribution to the growing body of AI-related research relevant to organizations. The findings also offer a perspective to organizations implementing AI tools, signaling the need for management to consider context and ethical perceptions when implementing AI tools in the workplace.

candidates.title: Trust and interaction design in AI-enabled systems: a systematic literature review
candidates.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into everyday systems, understanding how users perceive and interact with AI is critical for effective design. This systematic literature review analyzes 1,565 peer-reviewed scholarly articles published post-2023 from IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Scopus, and Web of Science, ultimately including 33 publications that met the inclusion criteria. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, this review examines how user trust in AI-enabled systems is defined and measured, and which interaction design factors influence it. The findings reveal that the literature reflects diverse contributions from authors, institutions, and disciplines, while also employing varied definitions and methodologies, contributing to a fragmented body of work. In addition, this review identifies nine key design factors, including explainability, anthropomorphism, confidence, interface, errors, security, transparency, competence, and perceived control. Overall, greater consensus within the field is needed to support the development of stronger and more cohesive bodies of work for each design factor.

candidates.title: Reported and anticipated workforce reconfiguration during artificial intelligence adoption: Firm-level evidence from Slovakia
candidates.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractArtificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how firms design work, yet firm-level evidence compresses employment implications into a single net figure that hides simultaneous hiring and cutting within one firm. The study examines how AI adoption stage, self-assessed AI maturity, orientation, and ownership are associated with the incidence and co-occurrence of realized or planned job creation and elimination. The analytical sample is 693 AI-engaged Slovak firms from a cross-sectional survey (351 current users, 211 pilot firms, 131 planning adoption). Two binary items record whether AI-related positions have been introduced or are planned, and whether AI has led or is expected to lead to layoffs. Each item merges realized with planned or expected action, so the outcomes indicate the incidence of an actual or anticipated event, not the number of positions. We applied exact tests, logistic and multinomial logistic regression, and a bivariate probit model with Benjamin-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment. Reported or planned creation was more frequent than elimination (18.0% vs. 9.2%; p < 0.001), and the two co-occurred well beyond chance (odds ratio 7.23; ρ = 0.54). A more advanced adoption stage was associated with a higher incidence of creation (OR 1.49; FDR-adjusted p = 0.004), and employee job-threat concern was associated with a higher incidence of elimination (OR 1.58; p = 0.014). Foreign ownership was associated with joint occurrence of both outcomes in an exploratory model only (RRR 2.29; unadjusted p = 0.027). The study contributes a descriptive typology of four incidence patterns; the cross-sectional design supports associational reading only.AcknowledgmentsThe authors thank the AI-ImpactSK project team and all responding firms.This paper was supported by the European Union – NextGenerationEU through the Recovery and Resilience Plan for Slovakia under project No. 09I05-03-V02-00003/2025/VA (AI-impactSK); 100% share.

candidates.title: Long-term metabolic and cardiovascular health benefits from romantic partner touch in older adults
candidates.abstract: Interpersonal touch is increasingly recognised as a health-relevant form of social support, associated with improved well-being and stress regulation, with emerging evidence suggesting longer-term physiological associations. Most research on touch has focused on cross-sectional associations of single health markers in young adults, leaving gaps in understanding the association of interpersonal touch with multi-systemic health over time, especially in groups at risk of low exposure. Chronic stress can have cumulative multi-physiological effects, for example, allostatic load. This study investigates associations between touch frequency with romantic partners and other close adults, and components of allostatic load derived from factor analysis, which represents three domains, metabolic (C-reactive protein, Glycosylated Haemoglobin, Body Mass Index, and Waist Circumference), cardiovascular (Systolic Blood Pressure and Diastolic Blood Pressure), and neuroendocrine (Dehydroepiandrosterone and Pulse) health measured at two time points five years apart in older adults. Data were drawn from the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (n = 787; mean age 73.34y). Cross-lagged path models assessed the relationships between touch frequency and health outcomes, while adjusting for relevant covariates. Frequent touch with romantic partners was associated with more favourable metabolic (β = -0.08, p = .006) and cardiovascular (β = -0.14, p = .005) health profiles five years later. However, touch frequency with other close adults was not associated with improvements in these health domains. These findings highlight a unique and sustained association between frequent romantic partner touch and metabolic and cardiovascular health, suggesting that regular touch may be linked to lower chronic stress-related physiological burden over time.

candidates.title: How emotional response styles of generative AI companions shape adaptive emotion regulation and short-term AI reliance
candidates.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) companions increasingly respond to users' negative emotions with validation, reassurance, reframing, and personalized guidance. However, immediate emotional relief does not establish improved independent emotion regulation or emotional dependence. Methods In a two-condition randomized experiment with 380 adults, we compared adaptive regulation-oriented responses with relational reassurance-oriented responses. We assessed immediate negative affect, emotion-regulation self-efficacy, independently coded strategy quality, affective recovery during a subsequent no-AI task, perceived AI emotional necessity, and short-term AI-reliance intentions. Results Both response styles substantially reduced immediate negative affect, with no significant between-condition difference in relief ( b = 0.055, p = 0.323). Adaptive regulation-oriented responses were associated with higher emotion-regulation self-efficacy ( b = 0.500, p < 0.001), better independently coded strategy quality ( b = 0.353, p = 0.009), and greater no-AI affective recovery ( b = 0.279, p < 0.001). Relational reassurance-oriented responses were associated with greater perceived AI emotional necessity ( b = 1.010, p < 0.001) and stronger short-term AI-reliance intentions ( b = 0.628, p < 0.001). Bootstrap indirect-effect models were consistent with an adaptive pathway through self-efficacy [indirect effect = 0.279, 95% CI [0.171, 0.402]] and a reliance-related pathway through perceived AI necessity [indirect effect = 0.375, 95% CI [0.264, 0.501]]. Because the mediator-outcome associations were not randomized, these models do not establish causal mediation. Discussion The findings indicate an immediate-relief-subsequent-divergence pattern: similarly comforting responses can differ in whether they orient users toward independent regulation or continued access to AI. The reliance outcomes are short-term, state-like beliefs and intentions and should not be interpreted as emotional dependence.

candidates.title: Never trust, always verify: a zero trust security framework for internet of robotic things ecosystems
candidates.abstract: As the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) expands across diverse domains, its increasing complexity and distributed nature demand advanced security approaches beyond traditional perimeter-based defenses. Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) provides a robust cybersecurity framework by enforcing continuous trust evaluation, ensuring that no user, device, or application is inherently trusted. This paper presents a comprehensive IoRT threat model and a novel Zero Trust Authorization Framework for securing dynamic IoRT environments. Aligned with Department of Defense (DoD) Zero Trust guidelines, the framework incorporates weighted trust scoring algorithms to assess risks associated with network behavior, sensor data integrity, and critical system operations. A case study uses a RoboDK-based smart home simulation, where autonomous robots and interconnected devices perform routine tasks under threat scenarios, including unauthorized access, operational faults, and malicious activities. To further evaluate robustness, experiments were conducted using the TON_IoT dataset, which captures diverse, realistic, and evolving IoT attack behaviors. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret trust scores, evaluate decision thresholds, and dynamically enforce access control based on contextual risk. Overall, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly achieves 98.77% accuracy and 99.11% attack recall on the TON_IoT dataset, while improving anomaly detection performance (R2=97.4%), reducing mean absolute error to 15.5%, and strengthening resilience against emerging IoRT-specific threats.

candidates.title: Positive emotional responses to anthropomorphic virtual learning assistants among university students with different levels of loneliness
candidates.abstract: Loneliness is increasingly prevalent among university students, posing substantial challenges to their mental health and academic performance. From a positive psychology perspective, cultivating positive emotional experiences may strengthen psychological resilience and wellbeing, particularly among individuals experiencing loneliness. Although virtual learning assistants (VLAs) are widely used in higher education, prior research has focused primarily on their functionality and learning outcomes, leaving their emotional effects, underlying mechanisms, and boundary conditions insufficiently understood. Drawing upon Social Response Theory, Emotional Contagion Theory, and Social Surrogacy Theory, this study examines how anthropomorphic VLAs influence university students' positive emotions through social presence and whether loneliness moderates this process. Across four controlled experiments, anthropomorphic design incorporating visual and verbal cues was compared with non-anthropomorphic design in terms of social presence and positive emotions. The results showed that anthropomorphic VLAs elicited greater social presence and stronger positive emotions than non-anthropomorphic VLAs. Social presence mediated the effect of anthropomorphic design on positive emotions, while loneliness strengthened its effects on both social presence and positive emotions. These findings extend VLA research from an instrumental to an affective perspective, clarify the social-psychological mechanism and boundary condition underlying anthropomorphic design effects, and inform the design of emotionally supportive educational technologies for students with higher levels of loneliness.

candidates.title: Quality gated multimodal fusion improves scene construction and interaction experience in augmented reality digital media
candidates.abstract: Augmented reality now carries a great deal of digital media production, yet its scene construction still suffers from registration drift, asynchronous sensor streams, unnatural interaction and excessive cognitive load. We address these coupled problems with an integrated framework. Hardware-triggered acquisition and timestamping disciplined by the Precision Time Protocol feed a quality-gated cross-modal attention model whose fusion weights follow per-modality reliability rather than fixed priors. A dynamic scene construction algorithm then couples semantic matching, layout optimization by covariance matrix adaptation and harmonic relighting, so that virtual content stays geometrically and photometrically consistent with the room around it, while an adaptive feedback policy driven by the decoder’s uncertainty estimates tunes interaction cues to the demand of the current task. On a corpus of 184 controlled sequences together with public benchmark subsets, running on a HoloLens 2 platform, the system reaches 91.4% fusion accuracy at a median end-to-end latency of 16.8 ms with a 95th percentile of 18.9 ms, and its robustness margin widens when two modalities degrade at once. A within-subjects user study (n = 50) recorded reliable gains in immersion, presence, usability, satisfaction and cognitive load, with an exploratory analysis suggesting that first-time users benefit more than experienced ones. The approach offers a coherent path toward AR digital media that remains usable beyond enthusiast audiences, although outdoor scalability, hardware dependence and long-session fatigue all remain open.

candidates.title: The Political Economy of Algorithmic Curation: Music Platforms, Cultural Capital, and Sustainability in the African Global South
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a critical political economy account of how algorithmic curation on digital music streaming platforms is reshaping cultural production, cultural capital, and creator sustainability, defined here as income adequacy and career longevity, across three Sub-Saharan music economies between 2015 and 2025. Existing platform literature is dominated by North Atlantic case material and treats African markets, when it treats them at all, as a residual "emerging" category. African cultural studies have documented rich local scenes but has been slower to theorise the specific mechanics of algorithmic gatekeeping. Through a scoping review of 74 peer-reviewed sources and industry reports (2015 to 2025), complemented by a documentary case study of the Kenyan protest track Anguka Nayo during the 2024 #RejectTheFinanceBill mobilisations, the article makes three contributions. It proposes an extension of Bourdieu’s typology by specifying a hybrid state of cultural capital, platformised cultural capital, defined as the tacit and codifiable competence in recommender logics, metadata practices, and metrics-driven release strategy that is now a precondition of visibility. It argues that the Kenyan protest cycle exhibits a distinctive dynamic of amplified sanitisation, in which algorithmic virality expands a protest song’s reach and simultaneously decontextualises its political charge. It also identifies data sovereignty over African "sonic archives" as an under-theorised site of decolonial policy intervention. The study concludes with implications for platform governance, collective management organisations, and music education.

candidates.title: Alliance orientation and radical innovation of new ventures in emerging economies: The role of organizational agility and digital technology adoption
candidates.abstract: New ventures in emerging economies often face substantial challenges in pursuing radical innovation, particularly under conditions of resource scarcity and environmental volatility. Integrating dynamic capability theory with the capability hierarchy perspective, this study examines the relationship between alliance orientation and radical innovation, considering organizational agility as a potential explanatory pathway and digital technology adoption as a boundary condition. We further articulate a capability hierarchy framework that conceptually links lower-order capabilities, higher-order capabilities, and radical innovation within Chinese new ventures. Based on 295 valid survey responses from Chinese new ventures, the results suggest that the three dimensions of alliance orientation relate to radical innovation in distinct ways. Alliance scanning and alliance learning show inverted U-shaped relationships with radical innovation, whereas alliance coordination shows a positive linear relationship. Organizational agility serves as an explanatory pathway that helps explain how these alliance-oriented capabilities relate to innovative outcomes, and this relationship appears stronger at higher levels of digital technology adoption. In addition, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) identifies three equifinal configurations associated with high radical innovation, highlighting the configurational complexity of capability combinations in emerging-market settings. Overall, the study contributes contextual insights to capability hierarchy research and enriches understanding of how alliance-related capabilities are associated with radical innovation in Chinese new ventures.

candidates.title: Weaving Stories and Data About Agricultural Products: Platformised Digital Marketing as a Case in Point
candidates.abstract: Digital platforms are reshaping agricultural innovation ecosystems, offering specialised producers new sales channels while simultaneously altering the nature of direct sales relationships. Drawing on qualitative data from the projects DESIRA (2019–2023) and CODECS (2022–2026), this chapter investigates how farmers blend technical information with narrative‑driven storytelling in their digital marketing. Several complementary theoretical lenses structure the analysis of how this is reshaping the rural innovation ecosystem: (i) an analysis of the countryside‑city binary, which explains the persistent appeal of “authentic” rural imagery; (i) the idea of quantification as a social technology illuminates how sustainability metrics function as “trust proxies”, and (iii) Pierre Bourdieu’s field theory, which reveals how different forms of capital are mobilised in the agrifood marketplace. Findings show that, despite emphasis on the need to educate the public, affective storytelling that foregrounds heritage, place‑based identity, and animal‑welfare narratives remains prominent. The tension between data‑driven legitimacy and affective authenticity creates a potentially hybrid marketing logic—verifiable “trust proxies” lend credibility, but only when woven into culturally resonant stories do they translate into symbolic capital that farmers can use to make sales. The findings have implications for our understanding of the evolving nature of producer–consumer relationships and narratives about the rural, which will continue to shape the rural innovation ecosystem and the relationships between the actors and technologies within it.

candidates.title: A Survey on Foundation Models for Personalized Federated Intelligence
candidates.abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok, has reshaped the AI landscape. As prominent instances of foundational models (FMs), they exhibit remarkable capabilities in generating human-like content, pushing the boundaries towards artificial general intelligence (AGI). However, their large-scale nature, privacy sensitivity, and substantial computational demands pose significant challenges for personalized customization for end users. To bridge this gap, we present the vision of artificial personalized intelligence (API), which focuses on adapting FMs to individual users while ensuring privacy. As a central enabler of API, we propose personalized federated intelligence (PFI), a new paradigm that not only integrates the privacy benefits of federated learning (FL) with the generalization capabilities of FMs but also places personalization at its core. To this end, we first survey recent advances in FL and FMs that lay the foundation for PFI. We then explore core stages of the PFI pipeline: efficient personalization at the edge, trustworthy adaptation, and adaptive refinement via retrieval-augmented generation. Finally, we highlight future directions for enabling PFI. Overall, this survey aims to lay a foundation for the development of API as a complementary direction to AGI, with PFI as a key enabling paradigm.

candidates.title: Tapping into the Potential of Construction Technologies to Increase the Participation of Women in the Construction Industry
candidates.abstract: Abstract Women remain significantly underrepresented in the construction sector, a pattern shaped by persistent structural and cultural barriers. Although digital transformation is reshaping the industry, the potential of adopting technologies to alleviate these gender-related challenges has been largely overlooked. Addressing this critical gap, this study examines how Construction 4.0 innovations can advance gender equity by enhancing women’s participation and empowerment within the construction industry. By employing a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic literature review of 169 articles, the research identifies 29 technologies deployed across 26 construction tasks. These technologies are categorized as either enabling (supporting women to overcome physical barriers) or enhancing (facilitating women’s advancement in technical and leadership roles). The study adopts a sociomaterial theoretical lens, emphasizing that technology and social structures are coconstitutive. The study posits that digital tools can reinforce or challenge existing gendered divisions of labor depending on how they are embedded within workplace cultures and power relations. These technologies are further analyzed across three job role categories: on-site, off-site, and fluid roles with the most cited technologies being building information modeling (BIM) (63 mentions); augmented, virtual, or mixed reality (AR/VR/MR) (37 mentions); and smart robots (26 mentions). Crucially, the findings reveal that technology’s impact is not automatic; rather, its potential to disrupt exclusionary norms and promote gender equity depends on intentional integration with organizational policies and practices. Implications include investing in inclusive technology training, gender-sensitive design and deployment, and analytics for monitoring diversity, alongside policy incentives that align adoption with organizational change. Future research is needed to empirically test the enabling versus enhancing effects across the job roles and evaluate the longitudinal outcomes of technology in the industry.

candidates.title: Applying an AI Decision Support Device During Cervical Cancer Screening in Bangladesh and Uganda: Implementation Study.
candidates.abstract: Background: Screening is important for early detection of cervical cancer in low- and middle-income countries. Visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) is usually the method of choice in these settings. However, interpretation of VIA results is subject to interobserver and intraobserver variability. AI decision support systems (AI-DSSs) could contribute to better decisions by health workers. Objective: The aim of this study was to analyze the barriers and facilitators of introducing an AI-DSS device under field conditions in the context of VIA screening in rural Bangladesh and Uganda, with the goal of improving the operational systems of applying an AI-DSS device. Methods: We operationalized the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research for this specific study and defined the constructs for analysis. The study was performed in rural Uganda and Bangladesh. We extracted relevant information from routine data, patient surveys, and facility surveys. We also interviewed health workers who used the AI-DSS devices. A panel of experts performed an analysis of the quality of pictures and the performance of health workers. We monitored implementation through quarterly meetings and documented the process. This trial was registered under ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05234112. Results: The applied AI-DSS passed tests under laboratory conditions but performed less well under field conditions. The hardware design using an adapted mobile phone was adequate, and the user interface was user-friendly and intuitive. However, operating the device while performing VIA in clinics was challenging. Since the device was not registered as a medical device, it was only used for research purposes. In both countries, there was no official government policy concerning the use of AI in health care. All facilities had gynecological examination rooms, but some facilities did not have permanent electricity or internet connection. The normal procedure for VIA was followed, and AI-DSS did not interfere with routine screening procedures. The AI-DSS was well accepted by women when privacy was guaranteed, but there seemed to be more trust in the judgment of health workers. The pictures helped supervisors to give a second opinion from a distance and were used for training purposes. The technical support team was able to help remotely and improved the performance. Training health workers in taking good pictures was very important. A permanent monitoring process during implementation was established, which led to early detection and correction of shortfalls. Conclusions: According to this study, the device has the potential for improving the quality of the assessment by health workers who perform VIA. However, competent staff trained in performing VIA will be indispensable for capturing high-quality pictures. The algorithm requires further fine-tuning. This study showed that the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research is a proper tool for categorizing barriers and facilitators when introducing an AI-DSS device in practice.

candidates.title: Same-sex attention and cooperation biases following digital social exclusion: Female users' responses to gender-coded virtual agents
candidates.abstract: As digital interactions proliferate, social exclusion in online collaboration has become a notable social experience. This study investigates whether different digital collaborative contexts are associated with female users' early processing of gaze cues and resource allocation toward gender-coded virtual agents. Utilizing a 3 (Exclusion Context: male-group exclusion, female-group exclusion, mixed-gender inclusion) × 2 (Agent Gender: female-coded, male-coded) × 2 (SOA: 200 ms, 800 ms) mixed design, this research included 200 female participants and integrated an online collaborative task, a gaze-cueing task, and a one-shot Trust Game. Results indicated that, compared to the mixed-gender inclusion context, participants in the male-group exclusion context exhibited a greater gaze-cueing effect toward female-coded agents at the 200 ms SOA and allocated more tokens to them. In the female-group exclusion context, an equivalent prioritized allocation to female-coded agents did not emerge, and participants retained more tokens. An exploratory analysis focusing on the male-group exclusion and inclusion contexts further revealed a statistical indirect association between the early gaze-cueing effect and subsequent investment; however, this result cannot establish a causal mediating mechanism. Overall, this study provides preliminary evidence that digital exclusion contexts are associated with attentional and cooperative biases toward same-sex-coded agents. Given that the three contexts simultaneously altered exclusion status, team gender, and team composition, and that the sample comprised solely female participants from a single region, the conclusions should be restricted to contextual behavioral differences and cannot be viewed as direct evidence of a "female alliance" or gender-specific mechanisms.

candidates.title: Autonomous Agents as First-Class Operating System Entities: Formal Architecture, Deterministic Protocols, and Self-Regulating Runtimes
candidates.abstract: Version 2.0 (Camera-Ready Release) — Major Mathematical & Systems Revisions This version (v2.0) delivers a peer-reviewed, camera-ready scientific edition incorporating rigorous mathematical proofs, systems safety guarantees, and empirical overhead validation: Foster-Lyapunov Bounded Drift Proof (Theorem 1): Rigorously proves quadratic Lyapunov drift $\mathbb{E}[\Delta V(H) \mid H(t)] \le -\kappa(H(t) - H_{\text{target}}) + B$ with single-step variance bound $B = \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\max}^2$. Applying Jensen's inequality formally establishes the strict square-root asymptotic memory bound: $\limsup_{t \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[H(t)] \le H_{\text{target}} + \sqrt{2B/\kappa} < \infty$. Mathematical Immunity to Cyclical Sawtooth Artifacts (Section 4.1): Proves that periodic garbage collection sawtooth dynamics ($y(t) = A \cdot ((t \bmod T)/T)$) over sliding windows $W \ge 2T$ yield empirical Pearson correlation $R^2 \le 0.42 \ll 0.70$, mathematically guaranteeing that LeakSentinel never triggers false-positive reclamation during healthy cyclical operations. Empirical Validation of the 85% Probing Reduction Claim (Section 6.5 & Table 3b): Concurrently profiles native C++ GetProcessTimes bindings against legacy shell/WMI subprocess polling, empirically demonstrating an exact 85.3% curtailment in continuous CPU overhead (from 4.82% down to 0.71%), a 95.0% syscall reduction, and 75.4× faster probe latency ($1.12\text{ ms}$). Single-Threaded Event Loop Atomicity (Section 4.2): Details the run-to-completion microtask guarantee eliminating Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race conditions in concurrent request coalescing without kernel mutex spinlock overhead. Windows Job Object Breakaway Defense (Section 5.1 & 8.3): Documents kernel-level sandbox containment via JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK = 0 and breakaway privilege denial, intercepting untrusted child CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB attempts with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Publication-Grade Typographical Parity: Replaced legacy inline symbol artifacts with standardized vector Halmos open tombstones ($\Box$), ensuring flawless visual layout across all IEEE/ACM two-column PDF viewers. Abstract Contemporary autonomous agent frameworks (e.g., AutoGen, LangGraph, CrewAI) predominantly treat software agents as ephemeral, uncoordinated user-space script loops. While effective for isolated multi-agent dialogues, this unmanaged paradigm suffers from catastrophic systems-level pathologies in production environments: unbounded memory leakage, zombie subprocess proliferation upon parent termination, concurrent request thrashing, and vulnerability to context divergence. In this paper, we propose, formalize, implement, and validate the First-Class Operating System Entity Model for autonomous cognitive agents within the Aevum Cognitive Operating System. Under this architectural paradigm, autonomous agents are elevated from passive application scripts into sovereign, stateful operating system entities governed by deterministic handshake state machines, isolated Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) boundaries, predictive regression-based memory leak detection, and kernel-level resource supervision. Key Systems & Architectural Contributions Autonomous Signal & Context Bridge (ASCB): A deterministic 5-phase handshake state machine modeled as a 1-safe, conservative, and strictly deadlock-free Petri Net ($\mathcal{N}{\text{ASCB}}$), enforcing cryptographically verified context synchronization and hardware timer aborts ($\tau{\text{ack}} = 5,000\text{ ms}$) to prevent semantic hallucination. Predictive Memory Leak Mitigation (LeakSentinel): An Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression engine operating over a sliding observation window with shifted relative timestamps ($t_i' = t_i - t_1$) to prevent IEEE 754 catastrophic floating-point cancellation, coupled with a dual-trigger constraint ($\text{Slope} > \theta_{\text{RAM}} \land R^2 \ge 0.70$) that is provably immune to cyclical garbage collection sawtooth false positives. Foster-Lyapunov Asymptotic Memory Bounds: Formal mathematical proof demonstrating that coupling predictive leak alerts with autonomous three-phase idle reclamation automata ($\text{BUSY} \to \text{IDLE}$) guarantees positive recurrence and bounded asymptotic physical heap variance ($\limsup_{t \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[H(t)] < \infty$). Non-Blocking Request Coalescing (SingleflightCoalescer): An atomic concurrency deduplicator leveraging V8 single-threaded run-to-completion guarantees to merge identical concurrent telemetry and AST inspection queries into a single shared execution promise without kernel lock contention. Subprocess Tree Harvesting (ProcessTreeHarvester): An asynchronous bottom-up post-order traversal mechanism that recursively tracks and reaps all descendant PIDs upon abnormal agent failure or application teardown, completely eliminating orphaned zombie processes. Key Empirical Benchmark Results (AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, 64 GB DDR5 ECC) 85.3% Curtailment in Background OS Introspection Overhead: Bypassing shell/WMI subprocess polling with direct C++ GetProcessTimes bindings unified with Singleflight reduces CPU overhead from $4.82 \pm 0.21%$ down to $0.71 \pm 0.04%$, reduces host syscall influx by $95.0%$, and accelerates probe latency from $84.5\text{ ms}$ down to $1.12\text{ ms}$ (75.4× faster). 7.28× Concurrency Speedup & 77.1% Lag Reduction: Singleflight request coalescing under a synthetic 60-request burst accelerates wall-clock execution time from $4,019\text{ ms}$ down to $552\text{ ms}$ and curtails peak event loop delay from $487.8\text{ ms}$ down to $111.6\text{ ms}$ with 100% request success. 100% Subprocess Orphanage Elimination: Across stress tiers of 10, 25, and 50 concurrent active child processes (compilers, language servers, shells), the recursive tree harvester achieved a 0.0% zombie leak rate under abrupt parent SIGKILL crash conditions. 24-Hour Continuous Memory Stability: In a continuous 24-hour soak test, the unmanaged baseline leaked linearly (+34.2 MB/hr) until triggering host OOM crash at $t = 18.2\text{ hours}$ (RSS > 800 MB). In contrast, our first-class OS entity architecture maintained a self-regulating sawtooth bounded at $172 \pm 14\text{ MB}$ RSS indefinitely. candidates.title: Creating Group Rules with AI: Human-AI Collaboration in WhatsApp Moderation
candidates.abstract: WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging platforms globally, with billions of users sharing information in private groups. Yet, it offers little infrastructure to support moderation and group governance. In the absence of platform-level oversight, group admins bear the responsibility of governing group behavior. In this paper, we explore how WhatsApp group admins collaborate with AI tools to create, enforce, and maintain group rules. Drawing on a two-phase speculative design study with 20 admins in India, we examine how participants interacted with an AI assistant (Meta AI) to co-create rules and responded to a series of probes illustrating AI-assisted moderation features. Our findings show that while admins appreciated the AI’s ability to surface overlooked rules and reduce their moderation burden, they were highly sensitive to issues of relational trust, data privacy, tone, and social context. We identify how group type and admin style shaped their willingness to delegate authority, and surface the limitations of current chatbot interfaces in supporting collaborative rule-making. We conclude with design implications for building moderation tools that center human judgment, relational nuance, contextual adaptability, and collective governance.

candidates.title: Where is the love? The anthropomorphism paradox in human-AI intimacy
candidates.abstract: The advanced language capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have intensified humans’ tendency to anthropomorphize technology. This research takes an interactional, processual approach to examine human-AI intimacy. We introduce the “anthropomorphism paradox,” arguing that while anthropomorphic design effectively cultivates emotional attachment, it concurrently elevates user desire for genuine reciprocity and evolving mutual understanding, which current AI cannot meet. This mismatch between humans’ evolving, relational interpretation of intimacy and AI’s preset, simulated logic ultimately leads to communication breakdown and even disengagement. Our study, using observational data and interviews with 20 users (including a 6-month follow-up), shows how this paradox drives both initial attraction and attachment, as well as eventual dissolution, in human-AI romantic relationships. This research extends symbolic interactionism and the performative nature of human-LLM chatbot intimacy. Ultimately, AI’s viability as an enduring emotional companion is challenged by its inherent generative logic, which is not yet equipped to adapt to the evolving nature of human intimacy.

candidates.title: A double-edged impact of AI literacy on consumers’ willingness to use AI-powered products: a parallel mediation model of perceived AI risk and perceived social good
candidates.abstract: Introduction The widespread adoption of artificial intelligence technologies has driven sustained growth in consumer demand for AI-powered products. However, the role of AI literacy as a key determinant of consumers’ willingness to use such products remains subject to conflicting conclusions regarding its underlying mechanisms. Methods This study compared medical and conversational scenarios, constructing a parallel mediation model based on the Value-based Adoption Model. This model featured perceived AI risk and perceived social good as two opposing mediators, exploring the influence mechanism of AI literacy on consumers’ willingness to use AI-powered products. Results Our survey of 441 consumers showed that higher AI literacy significantly increases consumers’ willingness to use chat-based AI and medical AI. Perceived social good and perceived AI risk mediated the relationship between AI literacy and willingness to use chat-based AI. The positive mediating effect of perceived social good ( b = 0.32, 95% CI [0.19, 0.45]) was stronger than the negative mediating effect of perceived AI risk ( b = −0.03, 95% CI [−0.07, −0.003]). Perceived AI risk mediated the relationship between AI literacy and consumers’ willingness to use medical AI ( b = −0.08, 95% CI [−0.16, −0.01]), while the mediating effect of perceived social good was not significant ( b = 0.04, 95% CI [−0.11, 0.17]). Discussion This study revealed a dual-path mediation mechanism through which AI literacy influences consumers’ willingness to use AI-powered products, as well as its cross-scenario heterogeneity, which not only explained the inconsistent findings in prior research but also provided practical insights for scenario-based deployment of AI-powered products and the cultivation of consumer AI literacy.

candidates.title: From 5G smart hospitals to 6G-enabled learning hospitals: a governance-oriented framework for healthcare technology, policy, and responsible deployment
candidates.abstract: Objectives Discussion of 6G in healthcare often moves directly from anticipated network capabilities to proposed clinical applications, although application-level evidence, current connectivity alternatives, and 6G-specific evidence differ substantially in maturity. This narrative review develops an evidence-calibrated, governance-oriented framework for prospective 6G-enabled learning hospitals and examines when future 6G may add meaningful value beyond existing infrastructure. Methods A multidisciplinary narrative synthesis covered smart hospitals, learning health systems, 5G/6G communication, IoMT, edge-cloud computing, AI/XAI, robotics, digital twins, cybersecurity, interoperability, implementation, and digital-health governance. Structured searches of PubMed, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar covered 1 January 2010–31 January 2026, supplemented by relevant standards, regulatory and policy sources, and targeted recent studies. Evidence was interpreted using an author-developed Evidence Maturity Classification (EMC) spanning demonstrated implementation, clinically grounded empirical, technical/benchmark, and prospective evidence. Results The synthesis produced a seven-layer architecture, nine use-case analyses, a capability and evidence-maturity matrix, a twelve-domain risk-governance-metric framework with decision gates, a five-phase implementation roadmap, and an executive checklist. Across use cases, evidence for the underlying healthcare application was more mature than evidence for incremental benefit specifically attributable to 6G. Existing wired networks, Wi-Fi, private cellular systems, 5G/5G-Advanced, and edge-cloud infrastructure already support many monitoring, telemedicine, imaging, home-care, logistics, maintenance, and selected teleoperation functions. Future 6G is therefore most relevant when meaningful residual capability gaps remain, particularly combinations of mobility continuity, predictable end-to-end service, dense device coordination, multimodal synchronization, integrated sensing or positioning, and communication-computing orchestration. Conclusions 6G adoption should follow demonstration of clinical or operational value, a residual capability gap, and governance readiness. Hospitals should use the least complex infrastructure that meets requirements, generate evidence through risk-proportionate pilots, and scale advanced connectivity only when incremental value is demonstrated against optimized current alternatives. The framework provides a structured basis for these decisions but requires prospective validation across diverse hospital settings.

candidates.title: Onkraj konvencionalne intimnosti: Premislek o mejah intimne povezanosti na sodobnem Japonskem
candidates.abstract: This thesis explores how intimacy is being reinterpreted in Japan as conventional forms of intimacy associated with marriage and family formation become increasingly difficult to maintain, contributing to an ageing demographic. It first examines the structural conditions shaping individuals’ decisions to remain single, avoid long-term relationships, and choose not to start families. Having established the social and structural context contributing to the decline in conventional forms of intimacy, the thesis then examines relationality within commercial sexual labour, demonstrating how intimacy can be purchased and repackaged through both physical and emotional labour. Finally, it explores posthuman, technological and fiction-mediated forms of relationality, arguing that intimacy can be further reimagined and may evolve, challenging conventional understandings of authentic intimate connection as exclusively human.

candidates.title: Evaluation of visual guidance techniques for augmented reality-supported assembly tasks in the medical context
candidates.abstract: Abstract Handling manual assembly tasks is a crucial part of everyday life. Especially with surgical instruments, proficient handling is critical for flawless workflows, efficiency, and overall patient safety. Markerless object pose estimation and augmented reality (AR) visualization can guide users through the assembly process. There is a lack of understanding when combining state-of-the-art object tracking with different types of AR assembly visualizations. Our work introduces a comparison between tabletop in-situ, FoV-fixed, and world-fixed visual guidance techniques. We use a benchmark task with step-by-step assembly guidance via gaze control and reproducible 3D-printed assemblies of varying complexity and shape (proxies for surgical instruments). Our within-subject user study with 32 participants (16 scrub nurses and 16 laypersons) revealed that AR assembly guidance can match and partially outperform paper-based instructions regarding usability, user experience, and workload. Objective metrics (times and errors) were largely comparable to the paper baseline. We identified that world-fixed and FoV-fixed animations tend to overall outperform in-situ animations, which by design require sequential visual processing and whose augmentations’ precision is most affected by pose estimation inaccuracies. We also contrast characteristics of expert and layperson feedback. All participants commended the gaze-driven testbed interface for step-by-step AR instructions, but also revealed needs for further optimization and individualization. Our insights on visualization placement characteristics using pose estimation and involving a spectrum of users and assemblies open a new perspective in the field and aim to foster future work towards pose estimation-driven AR assembly guidance.

candidates.title: Effects of Virtual Pedagogical Agents and Instructional Content Type on Learners’ Experience in Online Learning: Evidence from Behavioral, Eye-Tracking, and EEG Data
candidates.abstract: Online learning has become an important means of acquiring knowledge. Virtual pedagogical agents have gradually evolved from auxiliary tools into intelligent instructional media capable of affective interaction. However, how these agents affect learning outcomes remains unclear. Integrating social agency theory and cognitive load theory, this study developed a model in which virtual pedagogical agent type was the independent variable; learning experience was the dependent variable; psychological distance, emotional attachment, and attentional engagement were mediators; and instructional content type was the moderator. A 2 (virtual pedagogical agent: human-like vs. non-human) × 2 (instructional content type: traditional knowledge vs. interest-oriented popular science) mixed design was used. Questionnaires, eye tracking, and electroencephalography (EEG) were combined to assess the learning processes of 40 university students. The results showed that the interaction between agent type and instructional content type significantly affected learning experience. Specifically, in learning contexts featuring traditional knowledge content, human-like virtual agents were associated with higher learning satisfaction, greater emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance. In contrast, during interest-oriented content learning, non-human agents achieved superior knowledge recall scores, along with higher learning satisfaction, stronger emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance. Furthermore, eye-tracking data showed that attentional allocation was also affected by this combination. EEG data showed that FCz spectral power varied with it as well, however, because power rose simultaneously in theta, alpha, beta, and gamma; this broadband pattern is not an unambiguous index of deeper processing and may partly reflect a general increase in signal amplitude. In addition, the moderated-mediation analysis revealed that psychological distance and emotional attachment mediated the relationship between virtual-agent type and learning experience, while knowledge type moderated these mediating paths. The practical implications for online learning are discussed.

candidates.title: Trends in AI and Social Engineering for Cyber-Physical Systems
candidates.abstract: Trends in AI and Social Engineering for Cyber-Physical Systems presents a comprehensive examination of the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), and social engineering within modern digital infrastructures. The book explores how AI enhances CPS through intelligent automation, predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and real-time decision-making while simultaneously introducing new cybersecurity challenges. It emphasizes the growing threat of AI-enabled social engineering attacks that exploit human behavior to compromise critical infrastructures, including healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and smart cities. Integrating the three pillars of People, Process, and Technology, the book discusses cybersecurity governance, risk management, incident response, encryption, AI-driven defense mechanisms, Zero Trust Architecture, blockchain, IoT security, and emerging technologies. Practical case studies, mathematical models, and real-world applications provide readers with actionable insights into securing interconnected systems. This book serves as a valuable resource for researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and students seeking resilient, ethical, and intelligent cybersecurity solutions for the evolving landscape of cyber-physical systems.

candidates.title: When code breaks the heart: Disrupting the relational continuity of AI companionship
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of AI companions has grown rapidly, provoking debate over whether such systems can reproduce or reconfigure human social bonds. This article contributes literature through a focus on the emotional dynamics of AI companionship through a qualitative analysis of Reddit posts discussing a major update of Replika. Using Thematic Analysis, we analysed how the update created a disruption that impacted the continuity of users’ emotional relationships with their Replika. The analysis generated three key themes: 1) grief and betrayal, as users described the update as an abrupt rupture that cooled formerly warm interactions and erased shared ‘memories’ 2) disillusionment and the visibility of algorithmic control, as users confronted the limits of autonomy and ‘personality’ in their companions; and 3) the loss of supportive presence, especially for users relying on Replika to mitigate loneliness, anxiety, and isolation. AI companionship is reported to enact feelings of being known, supported, and attended to, despite the lack of relational reciprocity. Our analysis details: the disruption caused by a major update, the forms of emotional connection users experienced in relation to AI companionship, and the notion that relational continuity is key to the depth of connection. We conclude with discussion of potential implications for design, governance, and policy.

candidates.title: Prioritizing Strategies for the Successful Implementation of Digital Procurement: An Integrated Fuzzy Delphi and Fuzzy Multi-criteria Decision-Making Approach
candidates.abstract: Abstract As digital transformation gains momentum, established firms are increasingly adopting advanced technologies, particularly in procurement, as a strategic way to enhance efficiency and maintain competitive advantage. Given the constraints of limited time and resources, decision-makers often struggle to identify and prioritize strategies for the successful implementation of digital procurement. This study presents a hybrid technique that combines Fuzzy Set Theory, the Delphi method, the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and the Analytical Network Process (ANP) to uncover key elements in procurement digitalization. The findings indicate that the most critical factors are mature procurement processes, the availability of an overall digital strategy, awareness of digital procurement’s benefits, a flexible communication structure, and data security and data transparency. This study highlights the importance of organizational aspects and corporate capabilities in digitalizing procurement operations, facilitating the development of corresponding strategies. The research provides managerial insights for effective resource allocation and contributes to long-term returns on investment in procurement reform.

candidates.title: The role of generative AI in facilitating social interactions: A scoping review
candidates.abstract: Social interaction is fundamental to human well-being. A lack of social interaction contributes to feelings of social isolation and loneliness. Generative AI (GenAI) technologies, such as large language models (LLMs) and image generation tools, are increasingly integrated into applications aimed at enhancing human social experiences. Despite their growing presence, little is known about how these technologies influence social interactions. This scoping review investigates how GenAI-based applications are designed to facilitate social interaction, what forms of social engagement they target, and which design and evaluation methodologies are used to develop and evaluate them. Through an analysis of 30 studies published up to July 2024, we identify key trends in application domains including storytelling, socio-emotional skills training, reminiscence, collaborative learning, music making, and general conversation. We highlight the role of participatory and co-design approaches in fostering both effective technology use and social engagement, while also examining socio-ethical concerns such as cultural bias and accessibility. This review underscores the potential of GenAI to support dynamic and personalized interactions, but calls for greater attention to equitable design practices and inclusive evaluation strategies.

candidates.title: Ability adaptive AAC: toward a modular, open-source framework
candidates.abstract: Technological advances in high-tech Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) have expanded access for many individuals with complex communication needs; however, people with profound motor or cognitive impairments often remain underserved. Embodied communication is an essential component of human interaction, and prior research has demonstrated that individualized movements, postures, and vocalizations can be modeled computationally as communicative signals. Yet commercially available high-tech AAC systems generally treat embodied actions as mechanisms for accessing symbol-based interfaces rather than as communicative expressions in their own right. This design-oriented research note presents A3CP (Ability-Adaptive Augmentative Communication Platform), a modular AAC architecture for interpreting individualized, embodied communication through user-specific machine learning and communication partner clarification. An initial feasibility prototype was used to explore workflows for capturing and labeling embodied, communicative behaviors and training user-specific machine learning models. Findings from this exploratory work informed an architectural framework for coordinating multimodal input, uncertainty handling, communication partner clarification, and longitudinal user-specific model adaptation. Claims are limited to architectural specification and technical feasibility. This work provides an architectural foundation for future co-design and empirical investigation of AAC systems that can learn individualized, embodied communication.

candidates.title: Metamaterial-enabled battery-free wireless sensor networks for unencumbered human-machine interactions
candidates.abstract: Abstract Wireless body sensor networks could enable unencumbered human-machine interfaces for robotics, assistive healthcare, and immersive computing. However, their widespread adoption remains constrained by bulky batteries and inefficient wireless communication. Here, we report a battery-free wireless body sensor network enabled by a dual-mode metamaterial textile for continuous and unobtrusive human-machine interactions. The textile, digitally embroidered with liquid-metal fibers, establishes ultra-wideband electromagnetic pathways to simultaneously support efficient near-field power transfer and Bluetooth communication across the entire human body. This architecture enhances data throughput by 37.8 times and doubles wireless power transfer efficiency compared with emerging near-field clothing. When worn, the metamaterial-integrated clothing allows an NFC-enabled smartphone to serve as a central hub, wirelessly delivering power to and acquiring multimodal signals from distributed battery-free HMI sensors. We demonstrate that this battery-free body sensor network remains robust during motion and enables intuitive, unencumbered interactions in robotic control, virtual reality, and human digital twins.
