candidates.title: Medical Robot Motion Control: A Toolkit for Interactive, Patient-Specific Motion Planning in Medical Robotic Interventions
candidates.abstract: Motion planning is critical in medical robotics, helping keep robots safe from delicate anatomy during a procedure. Current research is limited by the lack of a common platform for both robot motion planning and medical image visualization, which complicates the development of patient-specific, supervised autonomous robotic workflows. To close this gap, we present the Medical Robot Motion Control (Motion Control) toolkit, which extends SlicerROS2, an existing interface between 3D Slicer and ROS2, with interactive kinematic solving and motion planning. The Motion Control toolkit lets users define goal poses, plan and preview trajectories around patient-specific anatomy, and execute those trajectories on physical hardware, all within 3D Slicer. We demonstrate the toolkit on two benchtop testbeds simulating a robot-guided lumbar spine intervention. On both platforms, the toolkit successfully planned and executed trajectories to 10 anatomical targets on a 3D-printed spine phantom. Additional trials showed that the toolkit reliably avoided the phantom when computing trajectories. These results demonstrate that the Motion Control toolkit provides a publicly available foundation for image-guided, patient-specific motion-planning research.

candidates.title: Obstacle avoidance for three-dimensional environmental robotic arms based on SGBM binocular stereo matching
candidates.abstract: Introduction In complex industrial operation environments, robotic arms need to achieve precise environmental perception and safe obstacle avoidance under the coexistence of occlusion, weak texture and dynamic obstacles. Methods To enhance the real-time performance and stability of three-dimensional spatial recognition, obstacle location, and path planning of robotic arms, a method for obstacle avoidance of three-dimensional environment robotic arms based on binocular stereo matching of semi-global block matching algorithm is constructed. Based on the 11th version of the real-time object detection network, the Convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, Semantic and Detail Interaction, Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network are introduced to enhance the nonlinear feature expression of obstacles, multi-scale fusion, and boundary positioning capabilities. Subsequently, the semi-global block matching algorithm is adopted to restore the binocular parallax and depth information, and the obstacle avoidance path planning is completed by combining the threedimensional point cloud of obstacles, the kinematic model of the robotic arm and the safety distance constraint. Results The average accuracy rate of the environmental detection model reached 98.21%, the precision rate reached 98.37%, the recall rate reached 97.42%, the positioning error was reduced to 1.26 cm, which was 1.58 cm less than that of the original detection model, and the frame rate still remained at 60.7, meeting the real-time detection requirements. In the three-dimensional obstacle avoidance experiment, the average path length of the proposed method was 1.83 m, the collision rate was reduced to 1.84%, the minimum safe distance was increased to 0.21 m, the average response time was only 48.3 m, the dynamic obstacle avoidance success rate reached 98.27%, and the task completion rate reached 98.64%. Discussion The research results show that this method can effectively improve the perception accuracy, path safety and dynamic obstacle avoidance stability of the robotic arm in complex three-dimensional environments.

candidates.title: Development of an artificial intelligence model to estimate psychiatrist-assessed mental health-related presenteeism
candidates.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to contribute to the development of an AI-based system that supports worker health and productivity by enabling early detection of presenteeism. We tested whether an AI model could assess mental health-related presenteeism with accuracy comparable to that of psychiatrists and whether the frequency of application use was comparable between avatar-based and real-person interfaces. METHODS: This study aimed to design a multivariable prediction model among white-collar employees in a Japanese company. The participants comprised 117 white-collar workers who provided a total of 1,631 video responses to a standardized health-status question over a period of 10 working days. The primary outcome measure was the accuracy of the AI model in estimating workers' mental health-related presenteeism. The secondary outcome was the frequency of application use when inquiring about workers' health conditions, comparing the avatar-based interface with the real-person interface. RESULTS: The AI model achieved an overall accuracy of 72.2%, a macro F1 score of 0.64, and a weighted F1 score of 0.73 compared with psychiatrists' ratings. Agreement between the two psychiatrists was 84.5%. Participants were allocated to either an avatar-based interface or a real-person interface, with no significant differences observed between groups in baseline characteristics or frequency of application use, whereas a significant difference was observed in the frequency of missing values. CONCLUSIONS: The developed AI model demonstrated performance comparable to psychiatrists in estimating mental health-related presenteeism from video data. This approach offers a novel, objective alternative to traditional questionnaire-based methods.

candidates.title: HeaTrace: A Parametric Design‐to‐Fabrication Workflow for Thermally Programmable Soft Robots
candidates.abstract: Inspired by the multifunctional bodies of natural organisms, soft robotic systems are advancing toward integrated body architectures that combine shape change, tunable compliance, and visual feedback within compact, material‐embedded structures. Thermal actuation provides a viable route to this multifunctionality by locally delivering heat from embedded Joule heaters to thermoresponsive materials. However, existing approaches treat heater geometry, conductive material, soft body design, and fabrication independently, limiting design flexibility and functional integration. This work presents HeaTrace, a design‐to‐fabrication workflow for thermally programmable soft robots that integrates parametric heater customization, a physics‐informed, semiempirical thermal model, and fabrication‐ready toolpaths for direct ink writing and automated fiber embedding. Controlled experiments on silicone substrates with embedded stainless‐steel yarn heaters quantify geometry and power‐dependent thermal performance from 5 to 15 W, heater durability, heat‐driven inflation, and stiffness modulation. The workflow is demonstrated through a gecko‐inspired soft robot achieving pump‐free inflation with a 6.5‐g thermally driven shape change actuator, a batoid‐inspired fin exhibiting 14% stroke asymmetry through programmable stiffness, and a humanoid face that expresses lifelike blushing. By integrating performance‐driven heater design with user‐defined functional materials and soft‐body geometries, HeaTrace opens a unified route to thermally programmable multifunctional soft robots.

candidates.title: Real-time environmental understanding through active classification using tactile sensing in robotic disassembly
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a generalized active classification framework designed to classify the environment of a robot through controlled tactile interaction, with direct application to robotic disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE). In this domain, purely vision-based systems frequently fail due to occlusions, dust, and reflective surfaces, making haptic identification an operational necessity. By formulating environment identification as an active sensing problem, we utilize the entropy of learned interaction models and a receding-horizon optimization to select control inputs that maximize information gain from force–torque feedback. Our approach transitions from a passive classifier to an active framework that dynamically probes the environment to resolve belief uncertainty across six distinct tactile classes, demonstrated through the high-precision detection and unfastening of screws using an industrial 6-DOF robotic arm. Experimental results on a consumer microwave demonstrate that the active framework achieves a 51% reduction in detection latency for screws compared to passive baselines and consistently outperforms expert-designed heuristics. Furthermore, the system exhibits robust zero-shot generalization to novel industrial objects, indicating that learned tactile signatures are invariant to the global object context. These results provide a scalable foundation for autonomous disassembly in high-variance environments like electronic waste recycling, while offering a broader methodology for any robotic classification task where control can be leveraged to accelerate information gain.

candidates.title: AI-Mediated Academic Labour and the Political Economy of Liberation: From Peer Review to Post-Labour Society
candidates.abstract: This paper uses the rapid automation of academic work as an empirical entry point for reconsidering labour and liberation under advanced artificial intelligence. Recent systems can mediate literature processing, idea generation, experimentation, manuscript writing, and peer review, while conferences are beginning to govern AI-generated evaluation and AI-mediated authorship at institutional scale. The paper distinguishes knowledge-generative activity from the circulatory, evaluative, administrative, and coordinative labour required to reproduce scholarly systems. It then examines whether automation can release scholars from compulsory functional roles while preserving self-directed participation in knowledge generation. Academic work is treated as a compact political economy in which production, verification, credit, scarce attention, resources, and institutional recognition interact. The resulting analysis extends beyond academia toward a broader post-labour question: liberation may concern the reorganization of compulsory functionalization and generative agency as much as the quantitative reduction of work.

candidates.title: Virtual sensing to enable real-time monitoring of inaccessible locations & unmeasurable parameters
candidates.abstract: Abstract Real-time monitoring of safety-critical interior states remains an open problem across energy, environmental, and industrial systems where direct instrumentation is infeasible. Existing approaches based on governing equations, discrete state vectors, or fixed sensor locations fail to provide mesh-independent, field-level reconstructions at arbitrary interior coordinates under real-time constraints. Here we introduce neural operator-based virtual sensing as a general framework for recovering inaccessible interior fields from sparse, heterogeneous measurements and operating conditions, instantiated with MIMONet, a multi-input, multi-output neural operator that fuses heterogeneous inputs and decodes coupled physical fields through a shared latent representation. Across three engineering-grade evaluations of escalating complexity, from confined recirculating flows to pressurized water reactor subchannels and compact power-system heat exchangers, MIMONet achieves ≤5% relative reconstruction error, while generating full-field predictions with sub-millisecond inference on an NVIDIA H200, at least five orders of magnitude faster than traditional high-fidelity CFD simulations, with calibrated uncertainty and noise resilience demonstrated on the heat-exchanger case. We validate the framework on three independent real-world datasets spanning electrochemical energy, atmospheric science, and physical oceanography: current-density mapping in a hydrogen fuel cell, wind-speed profiling on instrumented meteorological towers, and North Atlantic ocean-state from a global ocean reanalysis. MIMONet improves over classical virtual-sensing baselines by 72–84%: 84% on fuel-cell internal-field recovery from 10% sensor coverage and 83% on hub-height wind-speed recovery from lower-level tower sensors. Most notably, it recovers sea-surface height, a field with zero direct sensors, from its learned coupling to observed temperature and salinity at 4.1 × lower error than the best classical predictor, a cross-modal field recovery beyond the reach of classical interpolation. These results establish operator-based virtual sensing as a practical route to real-time field observability in systems where the states that matter most cannot be directly measured.

candidates.title: Netnographic Analysis of Audience Engagement with Netflix Türkiye's Instagram Promotions
candidates.abstract: Katılımcı kültür yaklaşımı çerçevesinde, dijital medya ortamları kullanıcıların yalnızca içerik tükettiği değil, aynı zamanda içerik üretimi, dolaşımı ve anlamlandırma süreçlerine aktif olarak katıldığı etkileşimli alanlara dönüşmüştür. Bu çalışma, sosyal medya platformlarında dijital film ve dizi tanıtımlarına yönelik izleyici etkileşimini incelemektedir. Araştırma, 01 Ocak 2026 ile 30 Mart 2026 tarihleri arasında Netflix Türkiye’nin resmi Instagram hesabında paylaşılan içeriklere yapılan kullanıcı yorumlarının netnografik analizine dayanmaktadır. Amaçlı örnekleme yöntemiyle seçilen 40 paylaşımın analizi, izleyici etkileşiminin yalnızca sayısal göstergelerle sınırlı olmadığını; aksine duygulanımsal tepkiler, katılımcı pratikler, eleştirel değerlendirmeler ve anlam üretim süreçleri tarafından şekillenen çok katmanlı bir yapıya sahip olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bulgular, etkileşimin öncelikle duygusal düzeyde kurulduğunu ve kullanıcıların içeriklerle güçlü bağlar geliştirdiğini göstermektedir. Kullanıcılar aynı zamanda yorumlar aracılığıyla aktif katılım sağlamakta, platforma yönelik taleplerini dile getirmekte ve kolektif etkileşim pratikleri geliştirmektedir. Çalışma, kullanıcıların oyunculuk performanslarını, anlatı yapılarını ve platform stratejilerini değerlendirerek birer gayri resmi eleştirmen gibi hareket ettiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Ayrıca fragmanlar, reels içerikleri ve oyuncu odaklı paylaşımlar gibi farklı içerik türlerinin farklı etkileşim biçimleri ürettiği belirlenmiştir. Bulgular, kullanıcı yorumlarının yalnızca tepkisel yanıtlarla sınırlı kalmadığını; aksine içeriklerin yeniden yorumlandığı, genişletildiği ve kolektif olarak anlamlandırıldığı bir alan oluşturduğunu göstermektedir.

candidates.title: A Student Guide to AI and Robotics
candidates.abstract: This book provides a practical and accessible introduction to AI and robotics, presenting the foundational technologies driving the development of intelligent systems. It covers key topics such as machine learning, perception, control, and autonomous decision-making, balancing theoretical concepts with practical applications. Through selected examples and case studies, the book explores robotics platforms and applied AI technologies used across industries, offering insights into their transformative potential in real-world scenarios. With a focus on hands-on learning, it introduces programming languages and tools commonly used in AI and robotics, empowering readers to apply concepts and techniques effectively. It also addresses the importance of building secure, responsible systems and examines the future of human-AI collaboration. An essential resource for introductory AI and robotics courses, this book provides the foundational knowledge needed to advance in these dynamic fields.

candidates.title: Label-free evaluation of state-of-the-art vision–language models on scenario understanding tasks: A case study in unstructured indoor construction sites
candidates.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising paradigm for zero-shot scenario understanding without task-specific training, yet existing benchmarks rely on costly manual annotation and generic scenes that fail to reflect the unstructured, dynamic nature of indoor construction sites. This case study introduces a label-free evaluation benchmark dataset, which comprises 1154 raw video clips captured from two real unstructured indoor construction sites in Xi’an, China. Nine state-of-the-art open-source VLMs are evaluated via five standardized prompt-driven tasks. The evaluation framework bypasses ground-truth annotations by introducing six proxy metrics (self-consistency, cross-model consensus, domain vocabulary coverage, hallucination suppression rate, structured parsing success, and inference efficiency) to objectively quantify model performance. Data collection and VLM inference are carried out collaboratively between a cloud server and the edge devices onboard the inspection robots, providing practical guidance on model selection for demand-driven construction scenario understanding tasks. The data and code are publicly available at https://github.com/redmogirill111/VLM-bench-for-indoor-construction-scenario-understanding .

candidates.title: Robotics and Agentic AI in Implant Dentistry. Clinician's Companion. First Edition, Part 1.
candidates.abstract: It’s an age of wonders in medicine and implant dentistry is not an exception. In addition, having moved into a fully digital treatment workflow, implantology is now spearheading innovation for dentistry. The pieces of the puzzle are falling together one by one: the digital patient, the digital treatment plan and now the digital execution with guided surgery and personalised prosthodontics. Personalised maintenance, digital monitoring and self-monitoring are also entering mainstream. Just like any era with rapid disruptive changes, education, standards and documentation lag behind the technology forefront. Clinicians today stand before an unprecedented potential to deliver better care with increased efficiency. At the same time, the challenge to navigate an ocean of devices, hardware and software is overwhelming. Manufacturers launch new devices and services at unprecedented speed, with conventional research unable to catch up. Devices and software line up promising to revolutionise the way we work. Distinguishing however between potential claims and true outcomes becomes increasingly difficult for a clinician. At the same time, parallel and often incompatible ecosystems are being developed from manufacturers, limiting clinicians choice. Inevitably, the main challenge we face today is not whether to use the technology or not, but rather how to efficiently combine the best devices and software in one meaningful, comprehensive and reliable workflow. Cybersmile, was our response to this need. The purpose remains to serve the patients with safer, faster, more efficient treatments, more predictable and better clinical outcomes. To that, technology remains a key, but it is a tool and not the purpose. Having tested countless devices and software in many combinations and having passed through all stages of enthusiasm and frustration, we decided that it was time to create an environment where colleagues can fast-track their learning, and grow competent in the technologies that deliver and the workflows that make sense for the patient and the clinic. This Clinician's Companion reflects exactly these principles and was initially written to accompany the CyberSmile signature Masterclass on Robotics and Agentic AI in Implant Dentistry. It is written for two readers at once: the experienced implant clinician who is meeting surgical robots for the first time and wants a structured account of what they are, how they work and where they fit; and the student or early-career dentist for whom this text is an introduction to computer-assisted implant surgery as a whole. We have deliberately started with the workflow, not the robot. Two decades of guided surgery have taught us that the accuracy of any execution method is bounded by the quality of the diagnosis and the plan that precede it. A robot placing an implant in a poorly planned position is an expensive way of making a mistake. Chapter 1 therefore lays out the digital clone and the digital treatment plan as the foundations on which everything else rests. Chapter 2 describes the robot itself as a medical textbook would describe an organ system: anatomy first, then physiology, then taxonomy. Chapter 3 applies the same anatomy and physiology to agentic AI, the software layer that is beginning to connect the fragmented digital workflow and could be the critical addition that helps robots to increase their autonomy in the future. Of all the technologies currently entering dentistry, this is the least understood and the one that could be the most disruptive. This chapter presents not only presents the anatomy and physiology but kickstarts the discussion of future potential and risk, a discussion which often borders with science fiction. The second part which is not included in this companion, is intended to offer deeper insights into more technical matters of advanced use, specific indications, zygomatic surgery and the economics of adopting these systems in practice. It is currently work in progress, but will soon be available at least in parts, as our educational offerings grow. Wherever possible we have used the terminology of the Glossary of Computer-Assisted Implant Surgery and Related Terms and the two companion workflow papers, so that this book is also an introduction to the language of the established scientific consensus. Each chapter opens with learning objectives and closes with summary points and a reference list, and the references are hyperlinked in the text so that the reader can go to the source. This is a first edition and in essence an early work in progress. The technology it describes is changing quickly and so does our experience with it. Some of the systems named will be superseded, while the evidence on some clinical outcomes is still thin. We would rather say so from start, than pretend otherwise. Not only we welcome corrections and suggestions from all readers - we will be actually thankful for – and they will find their way into the next edition, possibly coming out very soon Nikos Mattheos, James Chow and Alessandro Pozzi. Hong Kong, October 2026

candidates.title: MAGMA-GEN: Validated Recovery Supervision from Ambiguous Failures via Counterfactual Re-Execution
candidates.abstract: Hierarchical robotic systems executing long-horizon manipulation tasks must make high-level semantic decisions that orchestrate stochastic low-level skills. In this setting, failed rollouts are ambiguous: a poor downstream state may reflect an invalid high-level decision, partial observation, or a valid decision whose physical execution failed. Traditional supervised learning lacks data for such recovery states, while reinforcement learning struggles with sparse rewards and non-local credit assignment. We propose MAGMA-GEN, an on-policy data-generation pipeline that converts ambiguous failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision. MAGMA-GEN first uses a privileged coach to hypothesize an early decision-level error and propose localized correction or recovery actions. Because this diagnosis is fallible, candidates are retained only if re-execution from the same state under matched conditions improves downstream progress. This produces supervised examples from the agent's own failure distribution without per-step human demonstrations. Evaluated on interactive long-horizon manipulation tasks, MAGMA-GEN improves task success and recovery capabilities, against distillation and trajectory-repair baselines under evolving task constraints in both simulation and real-robot execution.

candidates.title: Continuum Robot Control Strategies: From Model-Driven to Embodied Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Continuum robots leverage intrinsic compliance and a high degree of freedom, making them well-suited for interaction in confined spaces. However, their distributed-parameter nature and pronounced nonlinearities pose major challenges for online closed-loop control. Guided by the origin of structural priors and by how control responsibilities are apportioned across the "brain-body-environment" loop, this survey charts the spectrum from model-driven control to embodied intelligence. Specifically, we organize model-driven control into physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid paradigms; summarize model-free control in terms of task-space feedback control, online mapping estimation, and input-output adaptive methods; and review embodied-intelligence control with an emphasis on morphological computation, distributed embodied sensing, policy learning and digital twins, and morphology-actuation-control co-design. This perspective provides a unified lens for synthesizing and comparing these three classes of control strategies.

candidates.title: Perspective Chapter: Multidisciplinary Perspectives in Social and Technological Innovations
candidates.abstract: The world is aging faster than ever before; the number of people aged over 65 years is projected to double from 2019 to 2050, hitting a record 1.5 billion. Aging is a multifaceted process, encompassing biological, social, and psychological factors, amongst others. An interdisciplinary approach that harnesses the power of social and technological innovations is needed to achieve holistic care for older persons. This chapter will highlight how the multidisciplinary teams in older adult care will include not only multidisciplinary medical teams but also social workers, community-based resources, and innovative technologies to cocreate person-centered innovations that empower older persons to live with dignity and independence.

candidates.title: On Estimating the Cardinality of Conjunctive Queries over Property Graph Databases for Query Planning
candidates.abstract: Cardinality estimation refers to the process of estimating the number of results that a query produces when executed on a dataset. Cardinality estimation plays a crucial role in query planning. Cardinality estimation errors can cause a query planner to choose execution plans that are far from optimal. The problem is scoped in two ways. First, this dissertation focuses on property graph databases, where data is modeled in a flexible form as graphs consisting of vertices, edges, labels, and properties. Second, this dissertation focuses on cardinality estimation for conjunctive queries, which is the core of most query languages. Many cardinality estimation techniques have been developed, both in industry and academia. Each has their own advantages and disadvantages. Different trade-offs lead to different performances in different scenarios. Having many different options, without an option that works well in all scenarios, naturally led to the existence of many different cardinality estimation techniques. This gave rise to the following two main research questions being investigated in this dissertation:- RQ1: How can we create structure in the wide range of currently existing cardinality estimation techniques that can be used to optimize conjunctive queries over property graph databases?- RQ2: How can we know when to use which cardinality estimation technique for optimizing conjunctive queries over property graph databases? A structured approach to this complex problem of cardinality estimation for query planning is developed through three main contributions:1. by defining a common notation based on probability theory;2. by developing a general framework;3. by providing an advisor tool. The first two contributions help towards answering RQ1 and the last one towards answering RQ2. A common notation helps communication, reduces the overhead of defining or understanding new notations, and provides a building block for the general framework. The common notation based on probability theory is given in Chapter 4.The general framework provides a modular approach to the cardinality estimation problem, stimulates new development, and simplifies comparisons. Chapter 5 explains the general framework, where the problem is divided into three distinct components: Partial Estimation Techniques (PETs), Extend Partial Estimate Set Techniques (EPESTs), and Combine Techniques (CT). New development can focus on one individual component at a time, and integrate it with existing solutions for the other components. This structure simplifies comparisons by clearly defining which components were kept stable and which were different. Many existing cardinality estimation techniques, or parts of them, are mapped to the different components of the framework. Chapter 6 shows experiments on different configurations of the framework, which highlight the parts of the estimation process that introduce the largest errors. The advisor tool, which is introduced in Chapter 7, provides evaluation assistance and scenario-specific optimizations. Given a specific scenario using a dataset and a query workload, the advisor tool shows a comparison of the performance of different cardinality estimation techniques. Chapter 8 demonstrates the advisor tool and shows that different scenarios require different cardinality estimation techniques to obtain the best results. Chapter 9 concludes this dissertation and discusses limitations and future work. By splitting existing techniques, categorizing them, and mapping them to the components of the general framework, structure is created in the wide range of currently existing cardinality estimation techniques (RQ1). No single configuration of the general framework performs the best in all scenarios. Complex relationships between 1) planning resources and cardinality estimation accuracy and between 2) cardinality estimation accuracy and execution resources required us to approach RQ2 on a case-by-case basis. The advisor tool takes a scenario (case) and provides comparisons of different cardinality estimation configurations for that scenario. Mapping out which configurations work best in common scenarios is part of future work. Eventually finding general guidelines would release the burden of finding or generating representative scenarios and running the advisor tool.

candidates.title: Overview Report: The Economic and Fiscal Implications of Alberta Separation
candidates.abstract: The Overview Report is based on extensive academic research and analysis by a number of Canada’s foremost economists and policy experts. It is a condensed picture the many different options, scenarios, factors and contingencies examined in greater detail and located separately within the Technical Papers collection that supports this summary.Development of this series reflects the contributions of a wide project team, including authors, reviewers, editors, research assistants and other research personnel, technical specialists and the integration and production group. The School gratefully acknowledges the expertise, time and care contributed by all those involved in the research, analysis, review, refinement and preparation of this work.

candidates.title: Quantified-self technology for enhancing social connectedness: a systematic review
candidates.abstract: Social connectedness plays a critical role in human health and well-being, yet increasing physical separation has contributed to rising social isolation and loneliness. Quantified Self (QS) technologies enable the continuous sharing of personal data and offer new opportunities to support connection at a distance. However, it remains unclear how QS technologies are designed and used to mediate social connectedness. This study systematically examines QS technologies from a design and contextual perspective through a literature review of 31 studies selected from Google Scholar, ACM, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed. The analysis is structured across six dimensions: data collection, design, context, design–context configurations, social connectedness measurement, and concerns. The findings show that current QS systems predominantly focus on strong-tie relationships in domestic settings, relying on physiological and activity data with primarily visual feedback. While low-attention and non-intrusive interaction is emerging, weaker ties, outdoor contexts, and multi-sensory modalities remain underexplored. Importantly, QS systems operate through recurring design–context configurations and support connectedness by reconstructing forms of co-presence at a distance. This review contributes a structured analytical framework and a configuration-level perspective, offering new insights into how self-tracked data mediate interpersonal connection and informing the design of socially aware, context-sensitive QS systems.

candidates.title: Leveraging design for collective phototaxis in morphological swarm robotics
candidates.abstract: Morphological computing-the use of a robot’s physical design to facilitate task execution-has emerged as a promising strategy in swarm robotics. Here, through experiments and simulations, we show that its success critically depends on both the robots’ control policy and the details of their physical design. We study a swarm of Kilobots embedded in an exoskeleton whose geometry controls the propensity of robots to align or anti-align with the external force they experience. Experimentally, the contrast between the two morphologies in the success rate of a simple phototactic task becomes dramatic when stopping is forbidden and robots can only slow down. Using a faithful physical model of the robots’ self-aligning dynamics, numerical simulations reveal that efficient phototaxis requires fine tuning of the self-alignment strength around a sweet spot. More broadly, varying this parameter unlocks a rich repertoire of collective behaviors. Careful design of robots morphology leverage interactions for collective behaviors from little computation as demonstrated through experimental realizations and faithful simulations of a swarm of robots performing phototaxis.

candidates.title: An adaptive method for land cover service composition based on service network
candidates.abstract: With the rapid advancement of emerging Internet technologies, the number and diversity of land cover services have increased substantially, leading to the development of an open land cover service ecosystem. Consequently, the automated orchestration of fine-grained services to construct land cover service chains has become an important research topic. However, Web-based land cover service composition environments are often subject to unpredictable anomalies, which may result in service execution failures or access interruptions. Therefore, an effective anomaly handling mechanism is essential to ensure the reliability and robustness of service composition. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an adaptive land cover service composition mechanism based on a service network. The proposed approach integrates land cover characteristics with service network properties to develop an adaptive model, an anomaly classification and decision-making framework, and an adaptive service composition algorithm. Furthermore, a Web-based land cover service composition system is implemented and evaluated through a land cover change detection case study. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves the success rate of service execution and enhances the adaptability and reliability of land cover service composition.

candidates.title: Uncertainty-aware model-enhanced soft actor-critic for conformal coating parameter optimization
candidates.abstract: Abstract Conformal coating optimization requires control of multiple application parameters to achieve target thickness and coverage uniformity, with spray atomization settings (atomization valve control) playing a crucial role in droplet formation and material deposition. Traditional manual tuning yields a low success rate and wastes significant materials through trial-and-error. We introduce Model-Enhanced Soft Actor-Critic (ME-SAC), a reinforcement learning approach that combines a hybrid dynamics model with uncertainty-aware planning. Our dynamics model integrates polynomial ridge regression with a residual neural ensemble, achieving R $$^{2}$$ = 0.70 using 5-fold cross-validation on the experimental dataset. Unlike conventional model-based RL that trains on synthetic data, ME-SAC uses the learned dynamics model for uncertainty-aware candidate-action evaluation without generating additional synthetic rollouts for replay-buffer augmentation. The RL agents are trained and evaluated through interactions with a surrogate coating environment constructed from 158 physical coating experiments. The planning module evaluates candidate actions using a conservative objective that penalizes high-uncertainty predictions, ensuring safe exploration. Experimental results demonstrate that ME-SAC achieves 95.0% success rate compared to 74.0% for model-free SAC baseline, reaching 90% performance using approximately 600 surrogate-environment interactions while baseline requires >1600 samples without achieving this threshold (>2.67 $$\times$$ sample efficiency). In the evaluated training runs, ME-SAC maintained performance without the mid-training degradation observed for the baseline.

candidates.title: From one tree to the canopy: an evolutionary design trajectory for tethered robotics in forest environments
candidates.abstract: Forest robotics has largely evolved along a ground-first and flight-dominant trajectory, treating the canopy as a region to observe or briefly access rather than a habitat to inhabit. In this Perspective, we propose an alternative canopy-first framework in which robots operate through anchoring, suspension, and tension-mediated interaction with the environment. We trace the progression from ground and aerial systems to perching mechanisms, identifying their shared limitation as transient canopy interaction. Tether-based robots instead enable sustained presence by transforming branches into structural supports. Within this context, TreeSpider is presented as an early canopy-innate morphology. We argue that such systems point toward a broader class of structure-innate robotics, where behavior emerges through physical coupling with the environment rather than continuous free-space mobility.

candidates.title: New visual culture of science: analysis of graphical abstracts in the life science journal “Cell”
candidates.abstract: Driven by the shift towards online journal publishing, many academic journals have introduced graphical abstracts (GAs) since the 2000s to convey the primary findings of research papers. This study investigated this visual culture in life sciences by analyzing GAs with focus on content, representation, and background. In total, 333 GAs were collected from articles published in the journal Cell in 2021 and analyzed. Among these, 295 GAs (88.6%) explained the results and models and succinctly presented the key findings, and 251 GAs (75.4%) used a layout that divided the area into two or more sections. New graphics that were not present in the main text were featured in 222 GAs (66.7%), indicating substantial investment in their creation. The GAs shared commonalities with modern infographics commonly seen on the internet, which emphasize clarity. The increased used of GAs may be attributed to the need for "instant comprehension," which is an epistemic virtue reinforced by authors, readers, and journals and driven by the scientific self of "surviving researchers and journals" in a competitive scientific environment.

candidates.title: Confucian institutional ethics: an informal constraint on corporate greenwashing
candidates.abstract: Amidst global efforts towards low-carbon transition and the increasing focus on corporate environmental responsibility, understanding the role of informal institutions becomes crucial. Positioning Confucian culture as an informal institutional factor, this study examines its impact on corporate greenwashing mitigation using panel data from Chinese listed firms between 2010 and 2024. Empirical results demonstrate that Confucian culture significantly inhibits corporate greenwashing, a conclusion supported by robustness and endogeneity tests. Furthermore, we identify the underlying mechanisms, including corporate social responsibility, managerial self-interest, and accounting information disclosure. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this inhibitory effect is particularly pronounced in regions with relatively weak Western cultural influence and formal rules. This study enriches upper echelons theory, imprinting theory, and social responsibility theory, providing empirical evidence for understanding how Confucian culture shapes corporate environmental decision-making. Collectively, it provides robust empirical evidence on the pivotal role of informal cultural institutions in guiding corporate environmental conduct and facilitating low-carbon transition.

candidates.title: Digital Romance and Intimacy Transformations among Chinese Rural Migrant Labourers
candidates.abstract: What are the intimate aspirations and everyday romantic lives of those who sustain China’s ‘world factory’? This book explores how digital dating platforms are reshaping relationships, partner selection and marriage among rural-to-urban migrant workers—a demographic that is often overlooked in studies of digital life. Drawing on 13 months of ethnographic fieldwork in Pearl River Delta factory towns, the study follows 62 migrant workers as they navigate love, desire and social expectations. It reveals how online dating creates new possibilities while also reinforcing existing inequalities. Platform features influence how users present themselves and form connections; however, family expectations, class divisions and gender norms still structure romantic choices. To explain this dynamic, the book introduces the concept of ‘digital capital’ to illustrate how familiarity with platforms and communication styles can improve relationship prospects while remaining unevenly distributed. Conducted roughly a decade ago, when platformisation was still in its early stages, the stories in this book now often feel strikingly romantic compared to the increasingly gentrified landscape of contemporary digital dating. This book will interest scholars and students of sociology, anthropology, digital media studies and gender studies, particularly those examining digital intimacy, social inequality, migration and contemporary Chinese society. It will also speak to readers who enjoy non-fiction love stories.

candidates.title: Roots or robots: futurizing Indigenous food sovereignty
candidates.abstract: We suggest how to futurize the Indigenous food sovereignty movements to influence, shape or confront future food technologies. Ensuring food security for the varied needs of humanity is an essential endeavor for existing food supply systems. The emergence of new, more sustainable food horticultural technologies is poised to be pivotal in the transformation of food systems. We captured the attitudes and perceptions of Māori, the Indigenous Peoples of Aotearoa New Zealand, through a series of focus groups exploring food technologies of Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA), Robotics and Automated Systems (RAS), and Genetic Editing (GE). Following thematic analysis, six values Continuums were identified: practices, produce, timing, power, environment and knowledge. We argue that the System of Six Values (SYS6) tool provides an Indigenous culturally grounded lens to encourage the consideration of multiple dimensions of food to navigate tensions between extractive technological modernization and rigid adherence to tradition.

candidates.title: Flexible control technology of industrial robot clusters: a survey
candidates.abstract: Manufacturing plants impose stringent requirements on the quality, efficiency and flexibility of batch production processes. Industrial robots, characterized by high flexibility, precision and reliability, have emerged as pivotal processing equipment in modern factories – particularly in the scenario of clustered flexible processing involving dozens or even hundreds of industrial robots. Through parallel collaboration among multi-robot systems and dynamic task allocation, not only can synchronous advancement of multiple manufacturing processes be achieved, but also equipment utilization efficiency and consistency of processing accuracy can be significantly improved, while enabling rapid switching of product processing procedures. Nevertheless, the current cluster control of industrial robots still suffers from several technical deficiencies. Specifically, the accuracy and real-time performance of collaborative control remain insufficient; the reliability and compatibility of communication links are compromised under conditions of high load, protocol heterogeneity and complex industrial environments; and the single-fault-tolerance mechanism may exert adverse impacts on production quality and efficiency. Against this backdrop, this paper reviews the research progress of industrial robot cluster control technologies in recent years, focusing on three core aspects: the robot cluster control framework, multi-robot collaborative control technologies, and anti-interference & fault-tolerance mechanisms. It systematically summarizes the characteristics, application scopes and existing limitations of these technologies, thereby providing valuable insights for the design and technical optimization of future industrial robot cluster control systems.

Implementation and user acceptance of a domestic robot-assisted surgical training system: a pilot educational study at the first clinical medical college of Jinan university
candidates.abstract: Objective Robot-assisted surgical systems are being increasingly utilized in the field of surgery, and have been reported to offer enhanced 3D visualization, force feedback, superior ergonomics for the surgeon, and improved operative precision, which collectively may contribute to minimally invasive outcomes and expedited postoperative recovery. However, the integration of robot-assisted technology into surgical training curricula in Chinese medical colleges remains limited. This pilot implementation study aims to evaluate the usability, acceptance, and perceived educational value of the Jingfeng Multi-port Robot-Assisted Surgical System in a structured surgical training program in China. Method The validity of the robot-assisted surgical system was first assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS). Participants then received practical training in applying the robotic technology to abdominal surgical procedures. Subsequently, a questionnaire was administered to collect their perceptions and evaluations regarding the integration of this technology into surgical practice. Result The mean SUS score was 80.58 ± 12.04. Questionnaire responses indicated positive participant perceptions regarding system usability and potential educational value, reflecting user acceptance rather than objectively measured educational effectiveness. Participants reported favorable views on perceived enhancements in learning efficiency, system characteristics, and ease of operation. Notably, male users gave significantly higher ratings (5.94 ± 1.26) than their female counterparts (4.78 ± 1.36) on the “Ease of operation” factor ( P = 0.011), suggesting a stronger perception of the system's user-friendliness among male participants. Conclusion In this observational pilot study, participants reported positive perceptions of the training mode, including perceived potential benefits for learning efficiency, motivation, and enjoyment. These perceptions do not establish causal effects of robotic training on educational outcomes.

BioOps : Enabling MLOps for scalable and flexible model‐centric process control in biopharmaceutical development
candidates.abstract: The deployment of advanced modeling and machine learning in biopharmaceutical process control has been limited by legacy fragmented automation infrastructure and a lack of model lifecycle governance. We present BioOps, a modular automation framework for biopharmaceutical advanced process control (APC). The framework incorporates established Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) principles, including version-controlled model registries, containerized deployment, and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines. BioOps explicitly decouples model development from model execution within the control architecture. This decoupling enables process scientists to deploy, test, and iteratively refine mathematical models and control strategies in a flexible manner. These workflows can be applied across heterogeneous bioreactor platforms and are executed entirely in-house, without reliance on vendor-specific solutions or custom system integration. In addition, BioOps embeds traceability, auditability, and model lifecycle management directly into the control stack. As a result, the framework aligns with regulatory expectations while continuing to support agile, in-house experimentation and development. Case studies across a geographically distributed set of bioreactors demonstrate BioOps' versatility in PAT-driven feedback control, hybrid model-based nutrient and glucose feeding, adaptive phase transitions, and cross-scale deployment. By operationalizing model-centric control through an MLOps-inspired architecture, BioOps provides a practical foundation for scalable, reproducible, and future-ready biomanufacturing.

candidates.title: Will AI save ethics—and make ethicists obsolete?
candidates.abstract: Abstract In 1982, Stephen Toulmin famously argued that medicine “saved the life of ethics.” This article asks whether AI is now doing something similar—and finds that the answer splits. Working from a broadly Toulminian conception of ethics as a discipline that responds to societal demand for normative orientation by providing analyses and reasoned recommendations, the article develops its argument in two stages. The first is diagnostic. AI is undeniably revitalizing ethics: it generates unprecedented demand for normative orientation and brings ethical questions to the center of public and academic debate. Yet AI appears to be on a trajectory toward becoming increasingly capable of supplying the very outputs for which ethicists have traditionally been consulted. If it can provide these outputs faster, more cheaply, and, in some respects, better, demand for ethics and demand for ethicists may increasingly come apart: ethics as a discipline may flourish even as ethicists as a profession face the prospect of becoming obsolete. In light of this diagnosis, the second stage asks how ethicists might respond. Four strategies are reconstructed: (1) defense and counterattack, (2) adaptive specialization, (3) ethics as an activity, and (4) cooperative transformation. Each strategy is critically assessed, culminating in a reflective appraisal of their respective strengths and limitations. The article concludes by arguing that ethicists must fundamentally reconsider the nature of their expertise and the role they can still claim for themselves in an age increasingly shaped by AI.

candidates.title: CoAdapt: An LLM-based Framework for Adaptive Collaborative Perception in IIoT Robotic Swarms
candidates.abstract: Industrial IoT environments increasingly deploy autonomous mobile robots for tasks such as material handling, product assembly, or infrastructure inspection. In such deployments, collaborative perception enables robots to share LiDAR observations and collectively construct a richer model of their environment than an individual agent could produce alone. However, industrial environments are dynamic spaces where robot positions shift continuously, network bandwidth fluctuates, and the marginal contribution of robots to perception quality varies at runtime. Existing collaborative perception approaches are designed for static participation assumptions and cannot adapt to these dynamics without sacrificing either detection precision or communication efficiency. This paper presents CoAdapt, an adaptive collaborative perception framework for IIoT robotic swarms in which a Large Language Model (LLM) serves as a runtime fusion controller, jointly deciding which robots participate in the fusion process and which fusion algorithm to apply based on the current spatial configuration and network state. The LLM reasons over structured natural language descriptions of the scene derived from raw LiDAR point clouds, requiring no taskspecific training and generalizing to unseen swarm topologies. Evaluated on the OPV2V benchmark across 25 scenarios, our approach achieves a 38% reduction in communication cost while maintaining detection precision comparable to static baseline approaches.

candidates.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. Here, we report an environmentally adaptive ionic actuator inspired by the Venus flytrap, capable of self‐sensing and bidirectional deformation without sustained external energy. By incorporating azobenzene moieties into an ionogel network, we trigger a unique nanopore‐mediated Janus actuation. A single, low‐power UV pulse (35.3 mW cm −2 ) induces rapid photoisomerization and localized dehydration, forming surface nanopores that facilitate asymmetric moisture uptake. This structural reconfiguration drives directional bending that is passively maintained for over 10 min, which is an exceptionally long retention time compared to conventional soft actuators. Furthermore, electrification‐induced voltage signals enable zero‐bias proximity sensing. By integrating these synergistic characteristics, we demonstrate a biomimetic ionograsper that combines ion‐redistribution‐induced sensing with energy‐efficient light‐triggered actuation for sophisticated object manipulation. Overall, this work provides a robust strategy for developing multifunctional and power‐efficient soft robots capable of intelligent environmental interaction.

candidates.title: CRISP: A 3D printer-based platform for precision solution printing on paper-based substrates
candidates.abstract: The scalability of self-driving labs is currently limited by the high cost of automated liquid handling. To address this, we present a low-cost, open-source platform designed to function as a 'frugal twin' to serve as a programmable hardware node in automated labs. To do this, we modified a commercial Ender-3 3D printer to print solutions on flexible paper-based substrates using a custom syringe pump assembly. Our printer, CRISP (Controlled Robotic Inkjet Solution on Paper), is driven by the Ender's native stepper motor and G-code infrastructure, and dispenses reagents via disposable pipette tips. Our demonstration with printed dyes shows a reliability of 96.8% and 98.2% for positional accuracy and uniformity of droplet circularity, respectively, confirming the system's potential as a reliable low-cost module for automated research.

candidates.title: Smart Objects for Clinical Rehabilitation and Education: A Scoping Review of Design, Sensing, and Validation
candidates.abstract: Interaction with physical objects plays a key role in the development, assessment, and treatment of cognitive and motor skills across the lifespan. In recent years, this interaction has been enhanced by smart objects, namely everyday items augmented with embedded sensing, processing, and feedback capabilities. These objects enable objective behavioural data collection while preserving natural and engaging human–object interactions. However, the literature remains fragmented and often focused on specific applications or interaction paradigms. This scoping review provides an overview of smart objects developed for clinical and educational contexts, with intended uses including assessment, treatment, training, education, and data collection to support machine learning approaches. Forty-two studies published from 2010 up to the final search date of 29 June 2026 were analysed following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The review adopts a design- and hardware-oriented perspective, classifying smart objects according to physical shape, intended use, target population, and validation level. Particular attention is given to embedded electronic components, measured parameters, and the exploitation of sensing and feedback technologies during human–object interaction. By synthesising current solutions, this review highlights emerging trends, recurring limitations, and open challenges related to design choices, technological constraints, and experimental validation, supporting the development of robust, adaptable, and real-world-ready smart objects.

candidates.title: Professional gamers on Twitter/X: tweeting for change
candidates.abstract: Professional gamers play esports as an occupation and income source. As a group, limited attention has been paid to professional gamers and their online behaviour on social media platforms such as X. The purpose of this paper is to explore the reasons (or motivations) of professional gamers to use X from a Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT) perspective. This study used exploratory and qualitative methods to analyse 23,356 tweets of South African professional gamers taken from their X accounts using NVivo. This allows for research on the use of X in another cultural context. Social interaction, information sharing, and promotion were identified as motives, but in this study, the motives of personal opinions, entrepreneurship, and gaming issues were also identified. The use of tweets to highlight causes enables professional gamers to use the platform to impact the broader gaming community, society and media.

candidates.title: EXPRESS: No Driver, No Problem? Social Construction of Robotaxi Ethics in the United States and China
candidates.abstract: Robotaxis are transforming urban mobility while raising ethical concerns that extend beyond technical performance. Drawing on the social construction of technology, this study examines how ethical concerns about robotaxis vary across the United States and China. Study 1 analyzes social media content about Waymo on TikTok and Apollo Go on Douyin, identifying five shared concerns (safety, accountability, transparency, cybersecurity, and social isolation) and context-specific concerns regarding vandalism in the United States and job displacement in China. Study 2 integrates innovation diffusion theory and Hofstede’s cultural dimensions theory to examine the associations among techno-optimism, uncertainty avoidance, regulatory support, ethical concerns, and robotaxi acceptance. The findings reveal both shared and context-dependent patterns across the two countries. This study advances autonomous mobility research by conceptualizing robotaxi ethics as socially constructed and demonstrating how sociocultural and institutional contexts are associated with ethical interpretations and acceptance in urban tourism.

candidates.title: Rethinking Vanlife: Towards an Ethnography of Vandwelling in Western Europe
candidates.abstract: This thesis explores how people live life on the road, within vans, buses, and converted vehicles. Drawing on three months of ethnographic fieldwork in early 2025 amongst people living roadside in Europe, and two weeks of additional fieldwork in the United Kingdom, it examines how privilege, mobility, and labour intersect within and between these mobile communities. Frequently enabled by internet connectivity and widespread automobile usage, vanlifers and digital nomads are fashioning new configurations of work and dwelling that blur the lines between tourism and livelihood. Online representations of these lifestyles often celebrate boundless freedom, yet fieldwork conducted on site with interlocutors suggests that such mobility is heavily and unevenly distributed along lines of class, gender, and nationality. There is a strong connection to people utilizing their established privileges and leveraging these within extant regimes of transnational mobility. This study approaches vandwellers as inhabitants of both physical and epistemological edges, occupying borderlands while navigating complex bureaucratic and technological constraints. The diversity of experiences amongst the roadwellers who contributed to this thesis exemplifies the capacity of peripheries to function as generative sites wherein global inequalities, ecological pressures, and neoliberal fantasies of autonomy converge. The thesis illuminates these contemporary forms of mobility and unsettlement by tracing everyday lives, arguing against perceived misrepresentations of these communities in the public and academic spheres. By the conclusion of fieldwork, I came to understand the machine homes of the vandwellers as crucial laboratories for rethinking freedom, work, ecology, and belonging in an increasingly precarious age.

candidates.title: Dissociative Identity Disorder in Online Spaces
candidates.abstract: In this thesis, I look into how people with Dissociative Identity Disorder, it sister disorder, or a similar condition (known collectively as systems) describe and discuss their own experiences. Qualitative data was gathered through the collection of posts from Tumblr and YouTube. Differences between these two online communities are discussed as well as differences between the terminology used in these posts and that used in the academic literature. This thesis investigates how systems discuss their plurality on Tumblr and YouTube, what the differences are between these social networking sites, and why those differences might exist as well as how these discussions use activist affordances. The main themes of the posts were as follows: Community versus clinical terms, educational content, and fighting between groups, with fakeclaiming (a person making an accusation that someone is simply pretending to be a system) or the fear of fakeclaiming also showing up often. This psychological anthropology research is a unique contribution to the literature because of my focus on how systems talk about themselves rather than having a focus on the specialists or experts in the field.

PCC-Suite: A Collection of Open-Source Programs to Analyze and Visualize GNSS Antenna Calibration Values
candidates.abstract: PCC-Suite is a collection of open-source programs to analyse and visualise GNSS antenna calibration values, and to quantify what differences between two calibrations do to estimated geodetic parameters. Developed at the Institut für Erdmessung (IfE), Leibniz University Hannover. Phase Center Corrections (PCC) are mandatory for high-precision GNSS positioning: the antenna height is measured to the bottom of the antenna, but the signal is received inside it. There is no universally accepted ground truth for these corrections, and calibrations of the same antenna differ between facilities, between methods (anechoic chamber or field robot), and between epochs. Those differences are usually compared on the grid defined by the ANTEX format. PCC-Suite exists to answer what happens next: how do PCC differences (ΔPCC) at the grid level transfer into the parameters we actually estimate? The programs PCC-Explorer: the core component. Propagates a ΔPCC pattern through a least-squares adjustment and reports the impact on north, east, up, receiver clock and troposphere, for a single station, a regional or global grid, or along a kinematic trajectory. PCC-Viewer: inspects PCC and PCV patterns from one ANTEX file, or the ΔPCC between two, as stereographic plots and elevation profiles. ATX-Converter: converts between ANTEX v1.4 and v2.0, with antenna and signal filtering. ATX-Scanner: scans folders of ANTEX files and builds a searchable table of which calibrations you hold. RINEX-Masker: applies an obstruction mask to a RINEX file and shows the effect in skyplots and DOP plots. The mask can be drawn by hand or generated from a hemispherical photograph. RINEX-Adapter: corrects and completes RINEX header records, cuts a time window, and changes the sampling interval, also in batches. PCC-Suite Launcher: one window that starts whichever program you need. Each program is a standalone Windows executable. No installation and no Python are required, and each is released and versioned separately so you can take only the one you need. This record contains the launcher package; the individual programs are released as their own records in the same community. Deliberately simple. PCC-Explorer isolates the effect of ΔPCC and nothing else: no filter tuning, no outlier detection and no ambiguity resolution. That is what makes the predicted impact reproducible from the calibration files alone, without any observations. Compared against real PPP solutions of the same data, the predictions agree to within 0.75 mm in every component at EPN station RANT (Germany, φ ≈ 54.8°) and within 1.64 mm at NYAL (Ny-Ålesund, Norway, φ ≈ 79°).

candidates.title: An open-set hybrid CNN-TCN network for human action recognition with unknown action rejection in collaborative robot workspaces
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Open-set recognition capability is becoming necessary for collaborative robots because actual shop-floor dynamics do not always correspond to the fixed action classes used during training. Misclassification of unknown human motions may lead to inappropriate robot responses, whereas reliable rejection enables safer supervisory control. Methods: An open-set human action recognition framework is developed by combining a spatial Convolutional Neural Network encoder with a Temporal Convolutional Network-based temporal aggregation module and an unknown-action rejection gate based on open-set scoring. The framework is evaluated on the NTU RGB+D 120 dataset using cross-subject and cross-view protocols with held-out action classes. Results: The proposed framework achieves 93.20% and 91.00% top-1 accuracy under cross-subject and cross-view evaluation, respectively, with corresponding Macro-F1 scores of 88.40% and 86.20%. For open-set detection, it achieves an AUROC of 0.938 and an AUPR of 0.750, with a 5.00% false acceptance rate for unknown actions and a 91.82% true known-action acceptance rate. The system operates at 15.0 ms per window and 66 fps on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16 GB, with a model size of 42 MB. Discussion: The results demonstrate that calibrated unknown-action rejection can improve safety-aware human action recognition while retaining practical real-time performance for collaborative robot workspaces.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Can't Feel Me: Lower Perceived AI Perspective–Taking Impedes Human–AI Cooperation
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly autonomous, its interactions with humans increasingly resemble social relationships, giving rise to a novel form of cooperation—human–AI teaming. Drawing on social cognition theory, the present research examines how individuals’ perceived AI perspective–taking shapes their willingness to cooperate. Across five studies, we find that individuals are generally reluctant to cooperate with AI possessing partial decision‐making authority (Studies 1 and 2), and this reluctance is shaped by perceived AI perspective‐taking (Studies 3 and 4). When AI agents appear to accurately—or even slightly overestimate—the thoughts and feelings of individuals experiencing unfair situations, perceived AI perspective–taking increases, thereby enhancing their willingness to cooperate with AI (Study 5). These findings extend perspective–taking research from human–human to human–AI contexts, highlighting that cooperation with AI depends not only on instrumental outcomes but also on social–cognitive inferences about being understood, and suggesting that psychologically anthropomorphic design may foster more effective human–AI interaction.

Preschool children develop scientific inquiry skills through STEM based investigations
candidates.abstract: Curiosity-driven exploration plays a fundamental role in young children’s early encounters with science and supports the development of scientific inquiry skills in early childhood education. In recent years, constructivist and child-centered approaches have increasingly emphasized the importance of engaging children in active investigation processes. Within this perspective, project-based learning offers meaningful opportunities for children to explore real-life phenomena, ask questions, and construct knowledge through hands-on experiences. The present study aimed to examine how a project-based STEM learning process can support preschool children’s scientific inquiry skills through an investigation of ants as a natural phenomenon that emerged from children’s curiosity. The study was designed as a qualitative case study. The participants consisted of 21 preschool children aged 60–72 months attending a kindergarten in the city center of Uşak, Türkiye. Data were collected during the 2020–2021 academic year through structured observations, interviews conducted before and after the project implementation, and document analysis, including observation notes and visual materials documenting children’s activities. The project was implemented following the three phases of the project approach: initiation, fieldwork, and finalization. The findings indicate that the project-based STEM process encouraged children to ask questions, make observations, develop explanations, and engage in collaborative inquiry while exploring ants. The results also suggest that integrating natural phenomena into project-based STEM activities can effectively support preschool children’s curiosity, critical thinking, and early scientific inquiry skills. These findings highlight the importance of inquiry-oriented and project-based learning environments in early childhood science education and provide practical implications for educators seeking to foster young children’s engagement with scientific exploration.

candidates.title: Giving robots the intelligence to work beyond Earth
candidates.abstract: Giving robots the intelligence to work beyond Earth SpaceR develops artificial intelligence that enables robots to explore, service, assemble and operate autonomously across planetary and orbital missions. The future of space exploration will not be limited by launch capability – it will be defined by robotic intelligence. As humanity prepares for a permanent presence on the Moon and a rapidly expanding orbital economy, robots must become capable of making complex decisions, adapting to uncertain environments and safely interacting with the physical world with minimal human supervision. At the University of Luxembourg, the Space Robotics Research Group (SpaceR) is developing the artificial intelligence (AI) that will power this new generation of autonomous space systems. Since its foundation in 2020, the group has rapidly established itself as one of Europe’s leading centres for AI in space robotics, securing more than €12.5m in research funding, delivering over 30 competitive research projects, publishing more than 130 scientific papers, and building unique experimental facilities dedicated to advancing robotic autonomy beyond Earth.

candidates.title: Autonomous robotic operation controlled by wave-based neuromorphic hardware
candidates.abstract: Abstract Equipping robots with a physical, brain-inspired computing unit is a key step towards achieving true autonomy in intelligent machines; however, the practical realization of such neuromorphic hardware remains a major challenge. Because both software- and hardware-based spiking neural network approaches demand substantial training and energy consumption, an architecturally simple neuromorphic platform is required to enable scalable and energy-efficient robotics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate robotic control driven by a neuromorphic hardware based on physical wave interactions. Using a water-based experimental system that provides direct visual access to wave-network dynamics, we establish a wave-based reservoir computing framework that achieves near-perfect accuracy in robotic vehicle obstacle recognition, followed by real-time autonomous motion with obstacle avoidance controlled entirely by this wave-based hardware. Through micromagnetic simulations, we extend this concept to electrically excited spin waves in a magnetic nanodevice operating at gigahertz frequencies, outlining an approach toward solid-state robotic chips based on wave computing. These results position wave-based computation as a scalable and energy-efficient alternative to conventional digital neuromorphic architectures for next-generation intelligent machines.

candidates.title: Extending Seabed DAS Beyond Permanent Infrastructure: Redeployable Fiber Nodes with Passive Cable Storage, Robotic Placement, and Multi-Leg Sensing
candidates.abstract: Temporary seabed deployment of sensing fiber can extend distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) beyond the few locations served by permanent submarine cables. A previous note (Bakulin, 2026a) proposed laying disposable fiber on the seabed from a vessel or from an underwater vehicle that carries the fiber spool. This note moves the cable storage off the vehicle and onto a seabed-resident frame. The frame carries a compact DAS interrogator, batteries, and one or more passive figure-eight cable baskets pre-loaded with sensing cable. The baseline frame is placed on the seabed and later recovered by conventional means; the underwater vehicle, autonomous or remotely operated, performs the core deployment task - acquiring the free end of the cable and pulling it along a planned route while the passive basket pays it out without a powered subsea winch - and, in the baseline configuration, does not transport the node or operate a powered reel. The cable is not respooled subsea; frame and cable are recovered by conventional or ROV-supported means, and reloading, cable exchange and optical reconnection are done on deck. The note then describes how the sensing aperture of a single frame scales. Two or more baskets may be carried on one frame and laid in different directions. Legs may be served by a multi-port interrogator, or by a single interrogator port through a two-fiber cable with a far-end turnaround, so that the fiber runs out one leg, back to the frame, and out the next, placing several physical legs on one serial optical path. Using a conservative illustrative 10 km optical-path envelope - compact interrogators are publicly specified for sensing ranges up to 20 km — two 2 km legs (about 6 km of optical path) fit on one port, and three or four shorter legs would also fit; the optical penalties of the turnaround, the double pass and the far-end loss have not been measured for this configuration and are identified as open questions. The architecture separates conventional frame handling, robotic cable placement, and sensing into three independent pieces, each of which can be developed and de-risked on its own, and offers a low-hardware route to multi-leg seabed arrays that can be deployed, recorded, recovered and redeployed. Aperture then scales at two levels: within a node, through additional baskets, legs, ports or serial paths; and across a survey, through additional nodes - a modular array of distributed-fiber nodes rather than a single long sensing line. Because the frame is designed for intervention, the same architecture supports campaign, serviced and connected operating models. Concept note, September 2026. This note documents a concept-level architecture and possible variants developed prior to any BIRD Energy Center award. It builds on Bakulin (2026a) and includes further system-level contributions by Bakulin and Dupré. Nothing herein is a specification, commitment, or performance claim. No proprietary or confidential third-party information is knowingly disclosed. No external funding supported this work. Component technologies and associated background intellectual property remain with their respective owners. This note does not determine ownership, inventorship, or licensing rights in any underlying or future implementation.

No proprietary or confidential third-party information is knowingly disclosed. No external funding supported this work. candidates.title: Remote Actuation of Concentric Tube Robots Using Torque Cables
candidates.abstract: The precision and flexibility of Concentric Tube Robots (CTRs) makes them well-suited for delicate surgeries and complex tasks in constrained environments, such as minimally invasive procedures. However, traditional CTRs can be bulky, as actuation typically requires multiple motors directly connected to the individual tubes. To reduce the system’s footprint, this paper proposes and evaluates remote actuation (from 1 m away) of concentric tubes using torque cables. First, we investigate the theoretical framework influencing torque transmission. Second, on a two-tube, balanced pair CTR prototype, we demonstrate the method’s performance in terms of tracing target positions and overall teleoperation ability. This study highlights the advantages and challenges of remote actuation, addressing key considerations and trade-offs when implementing this approach, and, critically, allows for miniaturising CTRs to deploy them closer to the target site without being limited by bulky actuation units.
